## Overview

Package aria provides unstyled behavior hooks for building components: the interaction and accessibility that a button, a checkbox or a dialog needs, without a look. It follows React Aria (Adobe's behavior hooks, Apache-2.0): the same names, the same rules for pointers, keys and focus, translated to Tela's hooks and props. The styled components of package kit are built on it; use it directly to build your own.

### The pattern: options in, Props out

A hook takes an options struct and returns a struct. Its Props field is one tela.Prop that carries everything the hook needs on the element: event handlers, the ref, the role and the aria states. Give it to the element, and style the element from the other fields of the result:

```go
press := aria.UsePress(aria.PressOptions{
    OnPress:  func(e aria.PressEvent) { save() },
    Disabled: busy,
})
return Button(press.Props, Class("rounded-md px-3 py-1.5"),
    If(press.Pressed, Class("scale-95")), Text("Save"))
```

Props merges several props into one (core's MergeProps): the handlers of one event all run, in the order given, and the others (a class, a role) follow the same rules as props given one after the other. So hook props combine with your own props and with each other:

```go
ref := tela.UseElementRef() // see "One element, several hooks" below
btn := aria.UseButton(aria.ButtonOptions{Ref: ref})
hover := aria.UseHover(aria.HoverOptions{})
ring := aria.UseFocusRing(aria.FocusRingOptions{Ref: ref})
return Button(btn.Props, hover.Props, ring.Props,
    Class("rounded-md px-3 py-1.5 transition"),
    If(hover.Hovered, Class("bg-accent")),
    If(ring.FocusVisible, Class("ring-2 ring-primary")), ...)
```

The hooks are ordinary custom hooks (ADR-085): call them at the top level of a component, in the same order on every build.

### One element, several hooks: the ref

A few hooks need the element itself (press measures it to know when the pointer leaves, the focus ring asks the engine who has the focus) and attach a ref to it. An element has one ref, so when several hooks serve one element they must share it: make it once with tela.UseElementRef and give it to each hook as its Ref option. The hooks that need no ref (UseHover, UseOverlay) take none.

```go
ref := tela.UseElementRef()
btn := aria.UseButton(aria.ButtonOptions{Ref: ref, OnPress: func(aria.PressEvent) { save() }})
ring := aria.UseFocusRing(aria.FocusRingOptions{Ref: ref})
return Button(btn.Props, ring.Props, ...)
```

Two different refs on one element are a mistake that dev mode reports with a panic that names both call sites and this fix (outside dev mode the last one wins). That includes h.Ref(other) next to the props of a hook: use the Ref field of the hook's result instead, or pass the ref to the hook. The same ref twice is fine.

### Controlled and uncontrolled state

A hook that holds state keeps it itself by default (uncontrolled), and lets the caller keep it (controlled) when the caller passes a pointer to the value, next to the callback that asks for changes. The callback is also called for an uncontrolled control, to follow it:

```go
// Uncontrolled: DefaultSelected is the initial state.
box := aria.UseCheckbox(aria.ToggleOptions{DefaultSelected: true})
// Uncontrolled and notified: read the result's Selected, or listen.
box = aria.UseCheckbox(aria.ToggleOptions{OnChange: func(on bool) { save(on) }})
// Controlled: the caller keeps the state.
on, setOn := tela.UseState(false)
sw := aria.UseSwitch(aria.ToggleOptions{Selected: &on, OnChange: setOn.Set})
```

A controlled control shows what the caller passes: a change that the caller does not store is refused, as with any controlled field. The open state of the overlay hooks (OverlayTriggerOptions, MenuTriggerOptions and TooltipTriggerOptions) follows the same rule with Open, DefaultOpen and OnOpenChange.

### Hooks

Interactions: [`UsePress`](#func-usepress) (mouse, touch, pen and keyboard as one press), [`UseHover`](#func-usehover) (mouse and pen) and [`UseFocusRing`](#func-usefocusring) (the focus, and whether to show it). Focus: [`UseFocusScope`](#func-usefocusscope) (contain, restore and auto-focus the focus, and a [`FocusManager`](#type-focusmanager) that moves it). Controls: [`UseButton`](#func-usebutton) (which can submit or reset its Form), [`UseToggleButton`](#func-usetogglebutton), [`UseCheckbox`](#func-usecheckbox) and [`UseSwitch`](#func-useswitch), which add the role, the aria state, the tab stop and the toggle state to a press. Choices and ranges: [`UseRadioGroup`](#func-useradiogroup) (one checked radio, which the arrow keys move and check), [`UseToggleGroup`](#func-usetogglegroup) (a segmented control or a toolbar of toggle buttons), [`UseSlider`](#func-useslider) (one or more thumbs on a track, dragged by repainting), [`UseProgressBar`](#func-useprogressbar) and [`UseMeter`](#func-usemeter). Dates: [`UseCalendar`](#func-usecalendar) and [`UseRangeCalendar`](#func-userangecalendar), with the [`Date`](#type-date) type. Colors: [`UseColorState`](#func-usecolorstate) (the color that a picker shares, as an [`HSB`](#type-hsb) that keeps the hue), [`UseColorArea`](#func-usecolorarea), [`UseColorSlider`](#func-usecolorslider) and [`UseColorField`](#func-usecolorfield), with the [`HSB`](#type-hsb) and [`HSL`](#type-hsl) types, [`ToHSB`](#func-tohsb), [`ToHSL`](#func-tohsl), [`ParseHexColor`](#func-parsehexcolor) and [`FormatHexColor`](#func-formathexcolor). Positioning: [`UseFloating`](#func-usefloating).

Overlays: [`UseOverlay`](#func-useoverlay) (Escape and a press outside close the top overlay; a modal one makes the rest of the window inert), [`UseDialog`](#func-usedialog) (role, name and focus), [`UsePopover`](#func-usepopover) (a floating overlay next to its trigger), [`UseOverlayTrigger`](#func-useoverlaytrigger) (the open state and the trigger's props), [`UseMenuTrigger`](#func-usemenutrigger) (a trigger that opens with press, long press or keys) and [`UseTooltipTrigger`](#func-usetooltiptrigger) (hover and focus with React Aria's delays and warm-up).

Collections, keyed lists of items with a focused key and a selection: [`UseListBox`](#func-uselistbox), [`UseMenu`](#func-usemenu) (the menu of [`UseMenuTrigger`](#func-usemenutrigger)), [`UseTabs`](#func-usetabs), [`UseSelect`](#func-useselect) (a button that opens a list box) and [`UseCombobox`](#func-usecombobox) (a text field that filters one, with the [`Contains`](#func-contains) and [`StartsWith`](#func-startswith) filters), with the [`Selection`](#type-selection) type for what is selected.

### Overlays

An overlay is rendered by its owner, in a Portal and only while it is open; the hooks give the props. The trigger hook holds the state, the popover positions and dismisses, the dialog names and focuses, and they share the overlay element's ref:

```go
trig := aria.UseOverlayTrigger(aria.OverlayTriggerOptions{})
pop := aria.UsePopover(aria.PopoverOptions{
    Trigger: trig.Ref, Ref: trig.OverlayRef, Open: trig.Open, OnClose: trig.Close,
    Placement: "bottom-start", Offset: 4,
})
dlg := aria.UseDialog(aria.DialogOptions{Ref: trig.OverlayRef, AriaLabel: "Filters"})
return Fragment(
    Button(trig.TriggerProps, Text("Filters")),
    Portal(Presence(If(trig.Open,
        Div(pop.Props, dlg.Props, Exit("opacity-0"),
            Class("rounded-md border bg-popover p-4 transition starting:opacity-0"), ...)))))
```

To let an overlay fade out, render it inside a Presence with If and give it Exit classes and a transition (and the starting: variant for the entrance), as above. An exiting overlay is inert and off the overlay stack at once, so the page below works while it fades, a second Escape reaches the next overlay, and the hooks' Open value is already false.

Presses and Escape reach only the top overlay. What is opened from an overlay is inside it (a popover in a dialog, a tooltip on a button in a popover), in a Portal or not.

### Collections

A list box, a menu and a tab list are collections: the caller gives the keys of the items (any comparable type) on every build, and renders one element per key with the props of ItemProps(key). The hook keeps the focused key and the selection, moves the focus with the arrow keys, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown and typeahead, and selects with the pointer and the keyboard as React Aria does.

```go
lb := aria.UseListBox(aria.ListBoxOptions[string]{Keys: names, SelectionMode: "multiple"})
return Div(lb.Props, Range(len(names), func(i int) tela.Node {
    return Div(lb.ItemProps(names[i]), Key(names[i]),
        Class("aria-selected:bg-accent focus-visible:ring-2"), Text(names[i]))
}))
```

The selection is a [`Selection`](#type-selection), uncontrolled by default and controlled when the options hold a non-zero one:

```go
sel, setSel := tela.UseState(aria.SelectionOf("b"))
aria.ListBoxOptions[string]{Keys: names, SelectionMode: "multiple",
    Selected: sel, OnSelectionChange: setSel.Set}
```

The focus is roving (the focused item's element has it) unless ShouldUseVirtualFocus keeps it on the collection and marks the focused item with aria-activedescendant. Give the items of a long list to a h.VirtualList: keys that are not rendered can still be focused.

A select and a combobox put a list box in a popover next to a trigger or an input. They return the props of each of their elements; the popover goes in a Portal, only while Open, and the items are rendered from ListBox.ItemProps as in a list box:

```go
sel := aria.UseSelect(aria.SelectOptions[string]{Keys: fruit, Placeholder: "Pick one"})
cb := aria.UseCombobox(aria.ComboboxOptions[string]{Items: fruit, AriaLabel: "Fruit"})
```

### Radio groups, toggle groups and sliders

A radio group keeps one checked key, uncontrolled by default and controlled when Value points to the caller's state; the caller renders a Button per key with RadioProps(key), and a Label(For(RadioID(key))) names and checks it:

```go
g := aria.UseRadioGroup(aria.RadioGroupOptions[string]{Keys: plans, AriaLabel: "Plan"})
return Div(g.Props, Range(len(plans), func(i int) tela.Node {
    return Button(g.RadioProps(plans[i]), Key(plans[i]), Class("checked:bg-primary"), Text(plans[i]))
}))
```

A toggle group is the same with a [`Selection`](#type-selection): SelectionMode "single" (a radio group of toggle buttons) or "multiple" (a toolbar of aria-pressed buttons). A slider has one thumb per value; its ThumbPercent is read in a paint-phase closure, so that dragging repaints and does not build:

```go
s := aria.UseSlider(aria.SliderOptions{DefaultValues: []float64{20, 80}, AriaLabel: "Price"})
track := tela.UseSize(s.TrackRef)
return Div(s.Props, Div(s.TrackProps, Class("relative h-2 w-64 bg-muted"),
    Range(2, func(i int) tela.Node {
        return Div(s.ThumbProps(i), Key(i), Class("absolute size-5 -ml-2.5 rounded-full bg-primary"),
            Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (x, y float32) {
                return float32(s.ThumbPercent(i)) / 100 * track.Get().Width, 0
            })))
    })))
```

### Calendars

A calendar selects a date (or, with [`UseRangeCalendar`](#func-userangecalendar), a range of dates) in a month grid, with React Aria's keys and rules, in the Gregorian calendar and the locale of package i18n (month names, weekday names, the first day of the week). A day is a [`Date`](#type-date), a comparable value with no time zone; the zero Date is none. The caller renders the parts from the methods of the result: the heading and month buttons, the weekday headers, and one grid of Weeks per visible month with a CellProps per day, keyed by its date, and the grid keyed by its month:

```go
cal := aria.UseCalendar(aria.CalendarOptions{AriaLabel: "Birthday", Min: aria.Today()})
return Div(cal.Props,
    Button(cal.PrevProps(), Text("<")), H2(cal.HeadingProps(0), Text(cal.Heading(0))), Button(cal.NextProps(), Text(">")),
    Div(cal.GridProps(0), Key(cal.Month(0).String()),
        Map(cal.Weeks(0), func(week []aria.Date) tela.Node {
            return Div(cal.RowProps(), Key(week[0].String()), Class("flex"),
                Map(week, func(day aria.Date) tela.Node {
                    return Button(cal.CellProps(0, day), Key(day.String()), Text(cal.DayText(day)))
                }))
        })))
```

The selected date is uncontrolled by default and controlled when Value points to the caller's state, as everywhere in this package; so is the focused date, which decides the month on display.

### Colors

A color picker is a [`UseColorState`](#func-usecolorstate) that its parts share: an area ([`UseColorArea`](#func-usecolorarea): saturation along one axis, brightness along the other), sliders for the hue and the opacity ([`UseColorSlider`](#func-usecolorslider), whose TrackColors are the stops of the gradient behind the thumb) and a hex field ([`UseColorField`](#func-usecolorfield)). The state is the color the picker shows, uncontrolled by default and controlled when Value points to the caller's tela.Color; it keeps the color as an [`HSB`](#type-hsb), so that dragging through gray or black does not lose the hue. All the parts are made in one component, and dragging moves the thumbs by repainting, as a slider does:

```go
st := aria.UseColorState(aria.ColorStateOptions{DefaultValue: new(tela.Hex("#6366f1"))})
area := aria.UseColorArea(aria.ColorAreaOptions{State: st, AriaLabel: "Color"})
hue := aria.UseColorSlider(aria.ColorSliderOptions{State: st, Channel: aria.ColorHue})
hex := aria.UseColorField(aria.ColorFieldOptions{State: st, AriaLabel: "Hex"})
```

### Testing and agents

The roles and states the hooks set are the ones the aria snapshot shows: a checkbox made with [`UseCheckbox`](#func-usecheckbox) prints as `checkbox "Name" [checked]`, and telatest finds it with ByRole("checkbox", "Name").

## Constants

```go
const (
    // MenuTriggerInput opens the list when the user types (the default).
    MenuTriggerInput = "input"
    // MenuTriggerFocus opens it when the input gets the focus too, with
    // every item.
    MenuTriggerFocus = "focus"
    // MenuTriggerManual opens it only with ArrowDown, ArrowUp and the
    // toggle button.
    MenuTriggerManual = "manual"
)
```

The ways a combobox's menu opens ([`ComboboxOptions`](#type-comboboxoptions).MenuTrigger).

```go
const (
    // FocusFirst focuses the first item: the menu opened with the keyboard
    // (ArrowDown, Enter, Space), a long press or a virtual click.
    FocusFirst = "first"
    // FocusLast focuses the last item: the menu opened with ArrowUp.
    FocusLast = "last"
)
```

Where the focus goes when a menu opens ([`MenuTriggerResult`](#type-menutriggerresult).FocusStrategy).

```go
const (
    // DefaultTooltipDelay is TooltipTriggerOptions.Delay when it is zero.
    DefaultTooltipDelay = 1500 * time.Millisecond
    // DefaultTooltipCloseDelay is TooltipTriggerOptions.CloseDelay when it
    // is zero; it is also how long after the last tooltip closes the next
    // one still opens at once (the warm-up).
    DefaultTooltipCloseDelay = 500 * time.Millisecond
    // NoDelay as a delay of [TooltipTriggerOptions] opens or closes the
    // tooltip at once (the zero value stands for the default delay).
    NoDelay time.Duration = -1
)
```

The tooltip delays of React Aria: a tooltip opens 1.5 s after the pointer enters its trigger, and closes 0.5 s after it leaves.

## Functions

### func Contains

```go
func Contains(text, query string) bool
```

Contains reports whether text contains query anywhere, ignoring case and diacritics ("cafe" matches "Café"; React Aria's useFilter with the "base" sensitivity of its collator). An empty query matches everything.

**Example**

```go
fmt.Println(aria.Contains("São Paulo", "ao p"))
fmt.Println(aria.StartsWith("Zürich", "ZUR"))
fmt.Println(aria.EndsWith("Zürich", "ch"), aria.EndsWith("Zürich", "ürix"))
// Output:
// true
// true
// true false
```

### func EndsWith

```go
func EndsWith(text, query string) bool
```

EndsWith reports whether text ends with query, ignoring case and diacritics. An empty query matches everything.

### func FormatHexColor

```go
func FormatHexColor(c tela.Color, alpha bool) string
```

FormatHexColor returns c as "#rrggbb", in lower case with the components rounded to 8 bits and clamped to the sRGB gamut; with alpha it is "#rrggbbaa". [`ParseHexColor`](#func-parsehexcolor) reads it back.

### func ParseHexColor

```go
func ParseHexColor(s string) (tela.Color, error)
```

ParseHexColor parses a hex color as people type it: "#rgb", "#rgba", "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa", in any case, with or without the leading "#" and with surrounding spaces ignored. The error says what is wrong and is meant to be shown (or the input reverted).

```go
c, err := aria.ParseHexColor("#1e1e2e")
```

**Example**

```go
c, err := aria.ParseHexColor("1E1E2E")
fmt.Println(aria.FormatHexColor(c, false), err)
_, err = aria.ParseHexColor("#12345")
fmt.Println(err)
// Output:
// #1e1e2e <nil>
// aria: invalid hex color "#12345": expected 3, 4, 6 or 8 hex digits (#rgb, #rgba, #rrggbb or #rrggbbaa), got 5
```

### func StartsWith

```go
func StartsWith(text, query string) bool
```

StartsWith reports whether text starts with query, ignoring case and diacritics. An empty query matches everything.

## Types

### type ArrowOptions

```go
type ArrowOptions struct {
    // Padding keeps the arrow that many pixels from the corners of the
    // floating element (Floating UI's padding).
    Padding float32
}
```

ArrowOptions are the options of [`Arrow`](#func-arrow).

### type AutoPlacementOptions

```go
type AutoPlacementOptions struct {
    // Padding is the space to keep between the element and the edges of the
    // area it must stay in.
    Padding float32
    // CrossAxis also counts the overflow on the alignment axis when it
    // chooses among aligned placements.
    CrossAxis bool
    // Alignment restricts the choice to placements with that alignment
    // ("start" or "end").
    Alignment string
    // AllowedPlacements are the placements it chooses among; nil is all.
    AllowedPlacements []string
    // NoAutoAlignment stops it from choosing the other alignment when
    // Alignment is set.
    NoAutoAlignment bool
}
```

AutoPlacementOptions are the options of [`AutoPlacement`](#func-autoplacement); the zero value is Floating UI's defaults.

### type Available

```go
type Available struct {
    // Width and Height are the largest size the floating element's border
    // box can take without leaving the area it must stay in, on the side of
    // the anchor it is on (Floating UI's availableWidth and availableHeight).
    // Negative when there is no room at all.
    Width, Height float32
    // Rects are the rectangles of the anchor and the floating element.
    Rects Rects
    // Placement is the placement the size is computed for.
    Placement string
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Available is what [`Size`](#func-size) gives its apply function: the room the floating element has and the means to limit it.

#### func (Available) MaxHeight

```go
func (a Available) MaxHeight(h float32)
```

MaxHeight limits the floating element's border-box height to h, like [`Available.MaxWidth`](#func-available-maxwidth). An element with overflow-y-auto then scrolls its content.

#### func (Available) MaxWidth

```go
func (a Available) MaxWidth(w float32)
```

MaxWidth limits the floating element's border-box width to w: the smaller of w and the element's own max-width wins, and the element is laid out again within the frame. Not calling it removes the limit.

### type ButtonOptions

```go
type ButtonOptions struct {
    // OnPress is called when the button is pressed and released over it,
    // with Enter, with Space, or by a virtual click.
    OnPress func(PressEvent)
    // OnPressStart is called when a press begins.
    OnPressStart func(PressEvent)
    // OnPressEnd is called when a press ends, whether it counts or not.
    OnPressEnd func(PressEvent)
    // OnPressChange is called with true when a press starts and false when
    // it ends.
    OnPressChange func(pressed bool)
    // OnPressUp is called when the pointer or the key is released over the
    // button.
    OnPressUp func(PressEvent)
    // Disabled makes the button inert and disabled for styling and
    // assistive technologies (h.Disabled): it cannot be focused or
    // pressed, and the `disabled:` variants apply.
    Disabled bool
    // ShouldCancelOnPointerExit ends the press for good when the pointer
    // leaves the button.
    ShouldCancelOnPointerExit bool
    // PreventFocusOnPress keeps the focus where it is when the button is
    // pressed with a pointer.
    PreventFocusOnPress bool
    // Type is what pressing the button does to the Form that contains it,
    // as HTML's type attribute: "button" (the default) nothing,
    // "submit" submits the Form (OnSubmit) and "reset" resets it, after
    // OnPress has run. A press has this effect whatever the element is, a
    // Button or a Div, and so does ElementRef.Click on it. Another value
    // panics in dev mode with the closest valid one.
    Type string
    // Ref is the element's ref, for a hook that is used together with
    // others on one element (see the package documentation); the zero
    // value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

ButtonOptions configures [`UseButton`](#func-usebutton). The press fields are those of [`PressOptions`](#type-pressoptions).

### type ButtonResult

```go
type ButtonResult struct {
    // Props go to the element: everything [UsePress] returns, the
    // "button" role, a tab stop and the disabled state.
    Props tela.Prop
    // Pressed is true while the button is pressed.
    Pressed bool
    // Ref is the ref attached to the element by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

ButtonResult is what [`UseButton`](#func-usebutton) and [`UseToggleButton`](#func-usetogglebutton) return.

#### func UseButton

```go
func UseButton(o ButtonOptions) ButtonResult
```

UseButton returns the props that make an element a button (React Aria's useButton): [`UsePress`](#func-usepress) plus the "button" role, a tab stop and the disabled state. It works on a Button element and on any other, such as a Div or an A, that should behave as one.

```go
btn := aria.UseButton(aria.ButtonOptions{OnPress: func(aria.PressEvent) { save() }})
return Button(btn.Props, Class("rounded-md bg-primary px-3 py-1.5 text-primary-foreground"),
    If(btn.Pressed, Class("scale-95")), Text("Save"))
```

A Button that has the hook's props presses with Enter and Space. Like every press, it prevents the default action of the click, so the Form is not submitted or reset by the element's own activation: set Type to "submit" or "reset" and the hook does it when the press completes, on a Button or on any other element.

```go
save := aria.UseButton(aria.ButtonOptions{Type: "submit"})
return Form(OnSubmit(func(tela.SubmitEvent) { send() }),
    Div(save.Props, Class("rounded-md bg-primary px-3 py-1.5"), Text("Send")))
```

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    clicks, setClicks := tela.UseState(0)
    btn := aria.UseButton(aria.ButtonOptions{
        OnPress: func(aria.PressEvent) { setClicks.Update(func(n int) int { return n + 1 }) },
    })
    // A Div that is a button: role, tab stop and the press come with the hook.
    return Div(btn.Props, Class("rounded-md bg-primary px-3 py-1.5 text-primary-foreground"),
        If(btn.Pressed, Class("scale-95")), Textf("Clicked %d", clicks))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Clicked 0"))
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output: - button "Clicked 1"
```

**Example (submit)**

```go
// A Div made a button that submits its Form, as an HTML submit button
// does.
page := func() tela.Node {
    sent, setSent := tela.UseState(0)
    send := aria.UseButton(aria.ButtonOptions{Type: "submit"})
    return Form(OnSubmit(func(tela.SubmitEvent) { setSent.Update(func(n int) int { return n + 1 }) }),
        Div(send.Props, Class("rounded-md bg-primary px-3 py-1.5"), Text("Send")),
        Textf("Sent %d times", sent))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Send"))
app.Press("Enter")
app.ExpectText("Sent 2 times")
fmt.Println("submitted twice: mouse and Enter")
// Output: submitted twice: mouse and Enter
```

### type CalendarOptions

```go
type CalendarOptions struct {
    // Value points to the selected date of a controlled calendar; nil
    // leaves it to the hook.
    Value *Date
    // DefaultValue is the selected date of an uncontrolled calendar at the
    // start; the zero Date selects nothing.
    DefaultValue Date
    // OnValueChange is called with the date the user selects: how a
    // controlled calendar asks for the change, a notification for an
    // uncontrolled one. It is not called for the date that already is
    // selected.
    OnValueChange func(Date)
    // Min and Max bound the dates that can be focused or selected (both
    // included); the zero Date is no limit. Dates outside them are shown
    // disabled, and the buttons of PrevProps and NextProps are disabled
    // when no month is left in that direction. Min after Max panics in
    // dev mode.
    Min, Max Date
    // IsDateUnavailable marks dates that are shown but can not be
    // selected (booked days, holidays). As in React Aria they can still
    // be focused: the keys move over them and they have aria-disabled.
    IsDateUnavailable func(Date) bool
    // Disabled disables every date: none can be focused or selected.
    Disabled bool
    // ReadOnly keeps the dates focusable but not selectable (aria-readonly
    // on the grid).
    ReadOnly bool
    // FocusedDate points to the focused date of a controlled calendar,
    // the one with the tab stop; the month that shows it is on display.
    // nil leaves it to the hook.
    FocusedDate *Date
    // DefaultFocusedDate is the focused date of an uncontrolled calendar at
    // the start: else the selected date, else Today. It is limited to Min
    // and Max.
    DefaultFocusedDate Date
    // OnFocusChange is called with the date that becomes the focused one:
    // by keys, by focus, by a month button, by a pointer that previews a
    // range. For a controlled calendar it is how the change is asked for.
    OnFocusChange func(Date)
    // VisibleMonths is the number of months shown at once: 1 (the
    // default) to 12. The month buttons move by that many.
    VisibleMonths int
    // FirstDayOfWeek is the first column of the grid; nil takes the
    // locale's (i18n.FirstDayOfWeek: Sunday for en-US, Monday for de,
    // Saturday for ar-EG).
    FirstDayOfWeek *time.Weekday
    // FixedWeeks always shows six weeks per month, so the grid keeps its
    // height from month to month; else a month has the weeks it needs.
    FixedWeeks bool
    // Today is the date [CalendarResult.IsToday] reports; the zero Date is
    // the current day (aria.Today). Set it to make a test deterministic.
    Today Date
    // Locale is the BCP 47 tag of the names, the headings and the first
    // weekday; empty is the component's locale (i18n.UseFormatter).
    Locale string
    // Direction is "ltr" or "rtl": it swaps ArrowLeft and ArrowRight. Empty
    // is the locale's.
    Direction string
    // AriaLabel names the calendar ("Appointment date"); the visible range
    // ("October 2026") is appended, as React Aria does. Else AriaLabelledBy
    // names it.
    AriaLabel      string
    AriaLabelledBy tela.ElementRef
    // PreviousLabel and NextLabel are the accessible names of the month
    // buttons, "Previous" and "Next" by default. They are English unless
    // the caller translates them (with i18n.T).
    PreviousLabel, NextLabel string
    // Ref is the calendar element's ref, for a hook that is used together
    // with others on one element; the zero value makes the hook create
    // its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

CalendarOptions configures [`UseCalendar`](#func-usecalendar). Dates are [`Date`](#type-date) values, the zero Date meaning none.

The selected date is uncontrolled when Value is nil (the hook keeps it, starting at DefaultValue, or with nothing selected) and controlled when Value points to the caller's state: the calendar shows it and only asks OnValueChange for the next one, so a change the caller does not store is refused. OnValueChange is also called for an uncontrolled calendar. The focused date, which decides the month on show and the tab stop, follows the same rule with FocusedDate, DefaultFocusedDate and OnFocusChange.

```go
// Uncontrolled.
aria.CalendarOptions{AriaLabel: "Appointment date"}
// Controlled.
day, setDay := tela.UseState(aria.Date{})
aria.CalendarOptions{Value: &day, OnValueChange: setDay.Set, Min: aria.Today()}
```

### type CalendarResult

```go
type CalendarResult struct {
    // Props go to the calendar's element: the "application" role, its name
    // and the ref (React Aria's calendarProps).
    Props tela.Prop
    // Title is the heading of the whole visible range, month and year in
    // the locale's order ("October 2026", "October 2026 – November 2026"
    // with two months): what an app shows above a single grid, or announces.
    Title string
    // Value is the selected date of a single-date calendar, the zero Date
    // for none. Range is the selected range of a range calendar (while the
    // first date of a new one is chosen it is still the previous range).
    Value Date
    Range DateRange
    // FocusedDate is the date with the tab stop.
    FocusedDate Date
    // Ref is the ref attached to the calendar by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

CalendarResult is what [`UseCalendar`](#func-usecalendar) and [`UseRangeCalendar`](#func-userangecalendar) return. Its methods give the props and the data of each part of the calendar: the heading and the month buttons, the weekday headers, and one grid of weeks of cells per visible month (see [`UseCalendar`](#func-usecalendar) for how they fit together).

#### func UseCalendar

```go
func UseCalendar(o CalendarOptions) CalendarResult
```

UseCalendar holds the state of a calendar that selects one date and returns the props and data of its parts (React Aria's useCalendar, useCalendarGrid and useCalendarCell with react-stately's useCalendarState). The calendar is the Gregorian one; a date is a [`Date`](#type-date), and the names, the headings and the first day of the week come from package i18n.

The caller renders the calendar. Each part takes its props from the result. The cells are keyed by their date and each grid by its month, so that a month on display is a new grid whose cell for the focused date takes the focus as it mounts (a calendar without those keys still works: the hook focuses the cell after the build):

```go
cal := aria.UseCalendar(aria.CalendarOptions{AriaLabel: "Birthday"})
return Div(cal.Props, Class("w-64 p-3"),
    Div(Class("flex items-center justify-between"),
        Button(cal.PrevProps(), Text("<")),
        H2(cal.HeadingProps(0), Text(cal.Heading(0))),
        Button(cal.NextProps(), Text(">"))),
    Div(cal.GridProps(0), Key(cal.Month(0).String()),
        Div(cal.RowProps(), Class("grid grid-cols-7"),
            MapIndex(cal.WeekdayNames(i18n.NameShort), func(i int, name string) tela.Node {
                return Div(cal.ColumnHeaderProps(i), Key(name), Text(name))
            })),
        Map(cal.Weeks(0), func(week []aria.Date) tela.Node {
            return Div(cal.RowProps(), Key(week[0].String()), Class("grid grid-cols-7"),
                Map(week, func(day aria.Date) tela.Node {
                    return Button(cal.CellProps(0, day), Key(day.String()),
                        Class("aria-selected:bg-primary aria-selected:text-primary-foreground"),
                        If(cal.IsOutsideMonth(0, day), Class("opacity-50")),
                        Text(cal.DayText(day)))
                }))
        })))
```

A cell is one element, a focusable gridcell (the ARIA grid pattern): use a Button, which gives it a focus ring, and style the states from the `aria-selected:`, `aria-disabled:` and `focus-visible:` variants or from the queries of the result ([`CalendarResult.IsToday`](#func-calendarresult-istoday), [`CalendarResult.IsUnavailable`](#func-calendarresult-isunavailable)).

Keys, on a cell: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move the focus a day (swapped by a right-to-left Direction), ArrowUp and ArrowDown a week, PageUp and PageDown a month and with Shift a year (the day of the month is kept, or the last one), Home and End the first and last day of the week, Enter and Space select the date. The month on display follows the focus. Dates outside Min and Max can not be reached (the focus stops at the limit); unavailable dates can, and are not selectable.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var picked aria.Date
page := func() tela.Node {
    cal := aria.UseCalendar(aria.CalendarOptions{
        AriaLabel: "Appointment", Locale: "en-US",
        Today:         aria.Date{Year: 2026, Month: time.October, Day: 25},
        OnValueChange: func(day aria.Date) { picked = day },
    })
    return Div(cal.Props, Class("w-64 p-3"),
        Div(Class("flex items-center justify-between"),
            Button(cal.PrevProps(), Text("<")),
            H2(cal.HeadingProps(0), Text(cal.Heading(0))),
            Button(cal.NextProps(), Text(">"))),
        Div(cal.GridProps(0),
            Div(cal.RowProps(), Class("flex"),
                MapIndex(cal.WeekdayNames(i18n.NameShort), func(i int, name string) tela.Node {
                    return Div(cal.ColumnHeaderProps(i), Key(name), Class("w-8"), Text(name))
                })),
            Map(cal.Weeks(0), func(week []aria.Date) tela.Node {
                return Div(cal.RowProps(), Key(week[0].String()), Class("flex"),
                    Map(week, func(day aria.Date) tela.Node {
                        return Button(cal.CellProps(0, day), Key(day.String()),
                            Class("size-8 aria-selected:bg-primary aria-disabled:opacity-40"),
                            If(cal.IsOutsideMonth(0, day), Class("text-muted-foreground")),
                            Text(cal.DayText(day)))
                    }))
            })))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page, telatest.Size(300, 300))
// Tab reaches the grid at today's cell; the arrows move over the months,
// PageDown a month, Enter selects.
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("button", "Next"))
app.Press("Tab")
app.Press("ArrowRight")
app.Press("PageDown")
app.Press("Enter")
title, _, _ := strings.Cut(app.AriaSnapshot(), "\n")
fmt.Println(picked, title)
// Output:
// 2026-11-26 - application "Appointment, November 2026":
```

#### func UseRangeCalendar

```go
func UseRangeCalendar(o RangeCalendarOptions) CalendarResult
```

UseRangeCalendar is [`UseCalendar`](#func-usecalendar) for a range of dates (React Aria's useRangeCalendar with useRangeCalendarState). Selecting works in two steps: a press or Enter on a date anchors the range, and while it is anchored the pointer over a date, or the focus on it, previews the range between the anchor and that date (see [`CalendarResult.IsInRange`](#func-calendarresult-isinrange)); a second press completes the range, whichever end comes first, and calls OnValueChange. Escape cancels an anchored range. While anchored, dates beyond the nearest unavailable one are not selectable, unless AllowsNonContiguousRanges. The result is the same as a single calendar's; its Range is the selected range, and [`CalendarResult.Anchor`](#func-calendarresult-anchor) the first date of a range being chosen.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var stay aria.DateRange
page := func() tela.Node {
    cal := aria.UseRangeCalendar(aria.RangeCalendarOptions{
        AriaLabel: "Stay", Locale: "en-US",
        Today:         aria.Date{Year: 2026, Month: time.October, Day: 25},
        OnValueChange: func(r aria.DateRange) { stay = r },
    })
    return Div(cal.Props,
        Div(cal.GridProps(0),
            Map(cal.Weeks(0), func(week []aria.Date) tela.Node {
                return Div(cal.RowProps(), Key(week[0].String()), Class("flex"),
                    Map(week, func(day aria.Date) tela.Node {
                        return Button(cal.CellProps(0, day), Key(day.String()),
                            Class("size-8 aria-selected:bg-primary"), Text(cal.DayText(day)))
                    }))
            })))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page, telatest.Size(300, 300))
// The first press anchors, moving the focus previews, the second press
// completes the range.
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("gridcell", "Sunday, October 25, 2026"))
app.Press("Enter")
app.Press("ArrowDown")
app.Press("ArrowRight")
app.Press("Enter")
fmt.Println(stay.Start, stay.End)
// Output:
// 2026-10-25 2026-11-02
```

#### func (CalendarResult) Anchor

```go
func (r CalendarResult) Anchor() (Date, bool)
```

Anchor returns the first date of a range being chosen, and whether there is one.

#### func (CalendarResult) CellProps

```go
func (r CalendarResult) CellProps(i int, d Date) tela.Prop
```

CellProps returns the props of the cell of date d in the grid of month i (React Aria's useCalendarCell): the "gridcell" role, a name that is the full localized date ("Monday, October 5, 2026"), aria-selected, the disabled state, the ref, the tab stop (the focused date's cell in its own month only) and the handlers: a click or tap selects, the keys of [`UseCalendar`](#func-usecalendar) move the focus, and a pointer over a cell previews the range being chosen. A date outside Min and Max or a disabled calendar has the Disabled prop (it can not be focused); an unavailable one, aria-disabled only. Render the cell with a Button and give it Key(d.String()): the cell of the focused date is a new element when the month changes and takes the focus when it mounts.

#### func (CalendarResult) ColumnHeaderProps

```go
func (r CalendarResult) ColumnHeaderProps(i int) tela.Prop
```

ColumnHeaderProps returns the props of the header of column i (0 to 6): the "columnheader" role, named by the full weekday ("Monday") whatever the short text it shows.

#### func (CalendarResult) DayText

```go
func (r CalendarResult) DayText(d Date) string
```

DayText returns the day of the month of d as the locale writes numbers ("5", "٥").

#### func (CalendarResult) FirstDayOfWeek

```go
func (r CalendarResult) FirstDayOfWeek() time.Weekday
```

FirstDayOfWeek returns the first column's weekday.

#### func (CalendarResult) GridProps

```go
func (r CalendarResult) GridProps(i int) tela.Prop
```

GridProps returns the props of the grid of month i: the "grid" role, named by its heading, aria-readonly and, for a range calendar, aria-multiselectable.

#### func (CalendarResult) Heading

```go
func (r CalendarResult) Heading(i int) string
```

Heading returns the title of month i, month and year in the locale's order and form ("October 2026", "octubre de 2026", "2026年10月").

#### func (CalendarResult) HeadingProps

```go
func (r CalendarResult) HeadingProps(i int) tela.Prop
```

HeadingProps go to the element that shows [`CalendarResult.Heading`](#func-calendarresult-heading) of month i (an H2): the grid of that month is named by it.

#### func (CalendarResult) IsDisabled

```go
func (r CalendarResult) IsDisabled(d Date) bool
```

IsDisabled reports whether d can not be focused: the calendar is Disabled, or d is before Min or after Max.

#### func (CalendarResult) IsFocused

```go
func (r CalendarResult) IsFocused(d Date) bool
```

IsFocused reports whether d is the focused date and the focus is inside the calendar.

#### func (CalendarResult) IsInRange

```go
func (r CalendarResult) IsInRange(d Date) bool
```

IsInRange is [`CalendarResult.IsSelected`](#func-calendarresult-isselected) for a range calendar: whether d is in the range, its ends included; it is false for a single-date calendar. Style the ends with IsRangeStart and IsRangeEnd.

#### func (CalendarResult) IsOutsideMonth

```go
func (r CalendarResult) IsOutsideMonth(i int, d Date) bool
```

IsOutsideMonth reports whether d is not a day of month i on display: a date of the neighbouring months that fills the first or last week.

#### func (CalendarResult) IsRangeEnd

```go
func (r CalendarResult) IsRangeEnd(d Date) bool
```

IsRangeEnd reports whether d is the last date of the range.

#### func (CalendarResult) IsRangeStart

```go
func (r CalendarResult) IsRangeStart(d Date) bool
```

IsRangeStart reports whether d is the first date of the range.

```go
func (r CalendarResult) IsSelected(d Date) bool
```

IsSelected reports whether d is selected: the selected date, or a date of the selected range (while a range is being chosen, of the range between its anchor and the focused date).

#### func (CalendarResult) IsToday

```go
func (r CalendarResult) IsToday(d Date) bool
```

IsToday reports whether d is today (the Today option, else the current day).

#### func (CalendarResult) IsUnavailable

```go
func (r CalendarResult) IsUnavailable(d Date) bool
```

IsUnavailable reports whether d can not be selected: the caller's IsDateUnavailable, or, while a range is being chosen, a date beyond the nearest unavailable one.

#### func (CalendarResult) Month

```go
func (r CalendarResult) Month(i int) Date
```

Month returns the first day of month i (0 to Months()-1) on display.

#### func (CalendarResult) Months

```go
func (r CalendarResult) Months() int
```

Months returns the number of months on display.

#### func (CalendarResult) NextDisabled

```go
func (r CalendarResult) NextDisabled() bool
```

NextDisabled reports whether the next button is disabled.

#### func (CalendarResult) NextProps

```go
func (r CalendarResult) NextProps() tela.Prop
```

NextProps is [`CalendarResult.PrevProps`](#func-calendarresult-prevprops) for the next month, disabled at Max (aria-label "Next").

```go
func (r CalendarResult) PrevDisabled() bool
```

```go
func (r CalendarResult) PrevProps() tela.Prop
```

PrevProps returns the props of the button that shows the previous month, or the previous VisibleMonths months (aria-label "Previous"): a click moves the months and the focused date back. It is disabled at Min. Give it to a Button.


WeekdayNames returns the names of the seven weekdays in the locale at the given width (i18n.NameShort: "Mo", i18n.NameNarrow: "M"), in the order of the columns: the first day of the week first.
