```go
func (r CalendarResult) Weeks(i int) [][]Date
```

Weeks returns the weeks of month i: rows of seven dates starting on the first day of the week, as many rows as the month needs (four to six), or six with FixedWeeks. The first and last rows hold dates of the neighbouring months, which [`CalendarResult.IsOutsideMonth`](#func-calendarresult-isoutsidemonth) reports.

### type Collection

```go
type Collection[K comparable] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Collection is what the collection hooks share: the state of the items (selected, focused, disabled), the props of an item and the way to move the focus. It is embedded in the results of [`UseListBox`](#func-uselistbox), [`UseMenu`](#func-usemenu) and [`UseTabs`](#func-usetabs).

#### func (Collection[K]) ActiveDescendant

```go
func (r Collection[K]) ActiveDescendant() tela.Prop
```

ActiveDescendant returns the aria-activedescendant prop that points to the focused item, for the element that has the focus when the focus is virtual and external; it is empty while no item is focused.

#### func (Collection[K]) ClearFocus

```go
func (r Collection[K]) ClearFocus()
```

ClearFocus forgets the focused key: no item is highlighted.

#### func (Collection[K]) Focus

```go
func (r Collection[K]) Focus(strategy string)
```

Focus focuses the first item ([`FocusFirst`](#constants)), the last ([`FocusLast`](#constants)), or the first selected one (the first when none is selected) for any other strategy, like the focus a Tab gives the collection.

#### func (Collection[K]) FocusKey

```go
func (r Collection[K]) FocusKey(k K)
```

FocusKey focuses the item with key k from a handler or an effect (a disabled or unknown key is ignored). With a roving focus the item's element takes the focus, scrolling a virtual list to it first when it is not rendered; with a virtual focus it becomes the highlighted item.

#### func (Collection[K]) Focused

```go
func (r Collection[K]) Focused() (K, bool)
```

Focused returns the focused key, and whether there is one (it is remembered after the focus leaves the collection, since it is the item that takes the focus when it comes back).

#### func (Collection[K]) HandleKeyDown

```go
func (r Collection[K]) HandleKeyDown(e tela.KeyboardEvent)
```

HandleKeyDown handles a key as the list's own handler does (navigation, selection, typeahead, Enter and Space on the focused item). Props already carries it; this is for another element that has the focus while the list is shown, as a combobox's input does with ExternalFocus.

**Example**

```go
// A list whose focus stays on a text field, as in a combobox: the
// field forwards its keys and carries aria-activedescendant.
names := []string{"apple", "banana", "cherry"}
page := func() tela.Node {
    lb := aria.UseListBox(aria.ListBoxOptions[string]{
        Keys: names, SelectionMode: "single", AriaLabel: "Fruit", ExternalFocus: true,
    })
    picked, _ := lb.Selected.First()
    return Div(
        Input(AriaLabel("Search"), OnKeyDown(lb.HandleKeyDown), lb.ActiveDescendant(),
            OnBlur(lb.ClearFocus)),
        Div(lb.Props, Range(len(names), func(i int) tela.Node {
            return Div(lb.ItemProps(names[i]), Key(names[i]), Class("h-8"), Text(names[i]))
        })),
        Textf("picked: %s", picked))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(300, 200))
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("textbox", "Search"))
app.Press("ArrowDown")
app.Press("ArrowDown")
app.Press("Enter")
app.ExpectText("picked: banana")
fmt.Println("picked: banana")
// Output: picked: banana
```

#### func (Collection[K]) IsDisabled

```go
func (r Collection[K]) IsDisabled(k K) bool
```

IsDisabled reports whether the item is in DisabledKeys.

#### func (Collection[K]) IsFocusVisible

```go
func (r Collection[K]) IsFocusVisible(k K) bool
```

IsFocusVisible is IsFocused for a focus that came with the keyboard: the item that should show a focus ring.

#### func (Collection[K]) IsFocused

```go
func (r Collection[K]) IsFocused(k K) bool
```

IsFocused reports whether the item is the focused one while the focus is in the collection: with a roving focus, the element that has the focus; with a virtual focus, the highlighted item.

#### func (Collection[K]) IsSelected

```go
func (r Collection[K]) IsSelected(k K) bool
```

IsSelected reports whether the item is selected (with [`All`](#func-all), every item that is not disabled).

#### func (Collection[K]) ItemProps

```go
func (r Collection[K]) ItemProps(k K) tela.Prop
```

ItemProps returns the props of the item with key k: its role (option, menuitem... by the hook), the aria state (aria-selected, aria-checked, aria-disabled), the ref, a tab stop (0 on the focused item, -1 on the others, none on a disabled one) and the pointer and focus handlers. Give every item of Keys its props, and the element a key of its own. An item element holds one ref: do not attach another (use [`Collection.ItemRef`](#func-collectionk-itemref)).

#### func (Collection[K]) ItemRef

```go
func (r Collection[K]) ItemRef(k K) tela.ElementRef
```

ItemRef returns the ref that ItemProps attaches to the item with key k, for measuring or focusing it; it has no element while the item is not rendered.

#### func (Collection[K]) Section

```go
func (r Collection[K]) Section(name string) SectionResult
```

Section returns the props of a group of items and of its heading (React Aria's useListBoxSection and useMenuSection). name identifies the section within the list; sections do not change the keys, which stay one flat list.

```go
fruit := lb.Section("fruit")
Div(fruit.Props,
    Div(fruit.HeadingProps, Class("text-xs text-muted-foreground"), Text("Fruit")),
    Div(lb.ItemProps("apple"), Key("apple"), Text("Apple")))
```

### type ColorAreaOptions

```go
type ColorAreaOptions struct {
    // State is the color the area changes, from [UseColorState]. It is
    // required, and must come from the same component.
    State *ColorState
    // XChannel and YChannel are the channels along the two axes: any two
    // of [ColorHue], [ColorSaturation] and [ColorBrightness] (the HSB
    // model), the third one stays as it is. The defaults are the picker's:
    // saturation along X and brightness along Y.
    XChannel, YChannel ColorChannel
    // Direction is "ltr" (the default) or "rtl", which mirrors the X axis
    // and the left and right arrow keys, as React Aria's area does.
    Direction string
    // Disabled makes the thumb inert and disabled, and the area ignores
    // presses.
    Disabled bool
    // OnChangeEnd is called with the color when the user stops changing
    // it: the pointer is released, or a key changed it.
    OnChangeEnd func(tela.Color)
    // FormatValue returns the text of a channel's value for aria-valuetext
    // and [ColorAreaResult.ValueText]; the default is English ("Saturation
    // 50%"). Use package i18n for another language.
    FormatValue func(ColorChannel, float64) string
    // AriaLabel names the area ("Color area" by default); else it is named
    // by AriaLabelledBy.
    AriaLabel string
    // AriaLabelledBy is the element that names the area.
    AriaLabelledBy tela.ElementRef
}
```

ColorAreaOptions configures [`UseColorArea`](#func-usecolorarea): a two-dimensional slider that changes two channels of the color at once.

### type ColorAreaResult

```go
type ColorAreaResult struct {
    // AreaProps go to the area element: the "group" role and its name,
    // and the handlers that make a press on it move the thumb to the
    // point and start dragging it, with a mouse, a finger or a pen.
    AreaProps tela.Prop
    // ThumbProps go to the thumb: the "slider" role (one for both
    // channels, as the semantics tree has no two-dimensional slider) with
    // the first channel's aria-valuenow and a value text that has both, a
    // tab stop, and the handlers: a press drags it (it keeps the grab, with
    // no jump), the arrow keys move it by one step (by a page with Shift,
    // mirrored in a "rtl" Direction), PageUp and PageDown change the Y
    // channel by a page, Home and End the X channel.
    ThumbProps tela.Prop
    // AreaRef and ThumbRef are the refs that the props attach.
    AreaRef, ThumbRef tela.ElementRef
    // Dragging is whether the thumb is being dragged, as of this build.
    Dragging bool
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

ColorAreaResult is what [`UseColorArea`](#func-usecolorarea) returns.

#### func UseColorArea

```go
func UseColorArea(o ColorAreaOptions) ColorAreaResult
```

UseColorArea holds the interaction of a color area (React Aria's useColorArea): a thumb in a rectangle, dragged with a pointer or moved with the keys, that changes two channels of the shared [`ColorState`](#type-colorstate). The caller renders the area (its background is the gradients of the hue, as the kit's does) and the thumb:

```go
st := aria.UseColorState(aria.ColorStateOptions{DefaultValue: new(tela.Hex("#6366f1"))})
area := aria.UseColorArea(aria.ColorAreaOptions{State: st, AriaLabel: "Color"})
size := tela.UseSize(area.AreaRef)
return Div(area.AreaProps, Class("relative size-48 rounded-md"),
    Style(tela.BgFn(func() tela.Color { return aria.HSB{H: st.LiveHSB().H, S: 100, B: 100, A: 1}.Color() })),
    Div(area.ThumbProps, Class("absolute -ml-2.5 -mt-2.5 size-5 rounded-full border-2 border-white"),
        Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (x, y float32) {
            px, py := area.ThumbPercent()
            return float32(px) / 100 * size.Get().Width, float32(py) / 100 * size.Get().Height
        }))))
```

Dragging moves the thumb by repainting only: like [`UseSlider`](#func-useslider), an uncontrolled color builds when the drag starts and ends and when the pointer rests, not on every move.

Unlike a slider's, the Home and End keys step the X channel by a page and PageUp and PageDown the Y channel, as React Aria's area does. The third channel (the hue, in the default area) is the state's: it is kept while the area moves the other two.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    st := aria.UseColorState(aria.ColorStateOptions{DefaultValue: new(aria.HSB{H: 220, S: 50, B: 50, A: 1}.Color())})
    area := aria.UseColorArea(aria.ColorAreaOptions{State: st, AriaLabel: "Color"})
    size := tela.UseSize(area.AreaRef)
    return Div(area.AreaProps, Class("relative size-48 rounded-md bg-muted"),
        Div(area.ThumbProps, Class("absolute left-0 top-0 -ml-2.5 -mt-2.5 size-5 rounded-full border-2 border-white"),
            Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (x, y float32) {
                px, py := area.ThumbPercent()
                sz := size.Get()
                return float32(px) / 100 * sz.Width, float32(py) / 100 * sz.Height
            }))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
thumb := telatest.ByRole("slider", "Color")
app.Focus(thumb)
app.Press("Shift+ArrowRight") // a page of saturation
app.Press("ArrowDown")
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Expect(thumb, telatest.HasValue("Saturation 60%, Brightness 49%"))
// Output:
// - group "Color":
//   - slider "Color"
```

#### func (ColorAreaResult) ThumbPercent

```go
func (r ColorAreaResult) ThumbPercent() (x, y float64)
```

ThumbPercent returns the position of the thumb in the area as it is now, in percent from the left edge (x) and from the top edge (y), 0 to 100: the X axis runs from the minimum of the X channel at the left to its maximum at the right (reversed in a "rtl" Direction) and the Y axis from the maximum at the top. It subscribes what reads it: read it in a paint-phase closure to place the thumb while it is dragged without building the component, as

```go
Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (x, y float32) {
    px, py := area.ThumbPercent()
    sz := size.Get()
    return float32(px) / 100 * sz.Width, float32(py) / 100 * sz.Height
}))
```

where size is tela.UseSize(area.AreaRef). Read in the component's body it makes the component build on every move.

#### func (ColorAreaResult) ValueText

```go
func (r ColorAreaResult) ValueText() string
```

ValueText returns the text of both channels as it is now ("Saturation 50%, Brightness 70%").

### type ColorChannel

```go
type ColorChannel string
```

ColorChannel names one component of a color, for the sliders and the areas that change it.

```go
const (
    // ColorHue is the hue, in degrees from 0 to 360.
    ColorHue ColorChannel = "hue"
    // ColorSaturation is the saturation, from 0 to 100.
    ColorSaturation ColorChannel = "saturation"
    // ColorBrightness is the brightness of the HSB model, from 0 to 100.
    ColorBrightness ColorChannel = "brightness"
    // ColorLightness is the lightness of the HSL model, from 0 to 100.
    ColorLightness ColorChannel = "lightness"
    // ColorAlpha is the opacity, from 0 to 1.
    ColorAlpha ColorChannel = "alpha"
)
```

The channels of the color hooks. Hue, saturation and brightness are those of [`HSB`](#type-hsb), saturation and lightness (in a "hsl" space) those of [`HSL`](#type-hsl), and alpha is the opacity.

### type ColorFieldOptions

```go
type ColorFieldOptions struct {
    // State is the color the field edits, from [UseColorState]. It is
    // required, and must come from the same component.
    State *ColorState
    // Alpha shows the opacity in the text ("#rrggbbaa"). Without it the
    // text is "#rrggbb" and a code of 3 or 6 digits keeps the opacity;
    // with it a code of 4 or 8 digits sets it too.
    Alpha bool
    // Disabled and ReadOnly stop the field from changing the color.
    Disabled, ReadOnly bool
    // AriaLabel names the field; else it is named by the element with
    // LabelProps, or by AriaLabelledBy.
    AriaLabel string
    // AriaLabelledBy is the element that names the field, when it is not
    // the one with LabelProps.
    AriaLabelledBy tela.ElementRef
    // Ref is the ref to attach to the input, to focus it from outside;
    // the hook makes one when it is zero.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

ColorFieldOptions configures [`UseColorField`](#func-usecolorfield): a text field for the hex code of the shared color.

### type ColorFieldResult

```go
type ColorFieldResult struct {
    // InputProps go to the Input: the text, the handlers and the name.
    InputProps tela.Prop
    // LabelProps go to the element that labels the field; a press on it
    // focuses the field.
    LabelProps tela.Prop
    // InputValue is the text of the input as of this build: what the user
    // is typing, or the color's code.
    InputValue string
    // Editing is whether the text is a draft that is not committed yet.
    Editing bool
    // Ref is the ref that InputProps attaches to the input.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

ColorFieldResult is what [`UseColorField`](#func-usecolorfield) returns.

#### func UseColorField

```go
func UseColorField(o ColorFieldOptions) ColorFieldResult
```

UseColorField holds a hex text field for the shared color (React Aria's useColorField). The user types a code ("#6366f1", "6366f1" or "#fff") and it is committed when the field loses the focus or on Enter: a code that parses sets the color, anything else (including an empty text) is reverted to the color's code. While the field is not being edited it shows the color, so a drag elsewhere in the picker updates it. ArrowUp and ArrowDown add or subtract one from the color as a 24-bit number, PageUp and PageDown sixteen.

```go
st := aria.UseColorState(aria.ColorStateOptions{DefaultValue: new(tela.Hex("#6366f1"))})
hex := aria.UseColorField(aria.ColorFieldOptions{State: st, AriaLabel: "Hex"})
return Input(hex.InputProps, Class("w-28 rounded-md border px-2 py-1 font-mono"))
```

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    st := aria.UseColorState(aria.ColorStateOptions{DefaultValue: new(tela.Hex("#6366f1"))})
    hex := aria.UseColorField(aria.ColorFieldOptions{State: st, AriaLabel: "Hex"})
    return Div(Class("p-4"),
        Input(hex.InputProps, Class("w-28 rounded-md border px-2 font-mono")),
        Span(Text("color "+aria.FormatHexColor(st.Color(), false))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
field := telatest.ByRole("textbox", "Hex")
app.Focus(field)
app.Press("Control+a")
app.Type("ff8800\n") // Enter commits; so does leaving the field
app.ExpectText("color #ff8800")
app.Press("Control+a")
app.Type("oops\n") // not a color: reverted
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - textbox "Hex": "#ff8800"
// - text: "color #ff8800"
```

### type ColorSliderOptions

```go
type ColorSliderOptions struct {
    // State is the color the slider changes, from [UseColorState]. It is
    // required, and must come from the same component.
    State *ColorState
    // Channel is the channel the slider changes. It is required:
    // [ColorHue] (0 to 360), [ColorAlpha] (0 to 1), [ColorSaturation] and
    // [ColorBrightness] (0 to 100), or [ColorLightness] with a "hsl"
    // Space.
    Channel ColorChannel
    // Space is the color model of the saturation and the lightness:
    // "hsb" (the default; it has a brightness) or "hsl" (it has a
    // lightness, and its saturation is not the HSB's). Hue and alpha are
    // the same in both.
    Space string
    // Orientation is "horizontal" (the default) or "vertical" (the minimum
    // at the bottom).
    Orientation string
    // Direction is "ltr" (the default) or "rtl", which mirrors a
    // horizontal slider and its arrow keys.
    Direction string
    // Disabled makes the thumb inert and disabled.
    Disabled bool
    // OnChangeEnd is called with the color when the user stops changing it.
    OnChangeEnd func(tela.Color)
    // FormatValue returns the text of the value for aria-valuetext and
    // [ColorSliderResult.ValueText]; the default is English ("Hue 180°",
    // "Alpha 80%"). Use package i18n for another language.
    FormatValue func(ColorChannel, float64) string
    // AriaLabel names the slider; the default is the channel's name
    // ("Hue"). A visible label is the slider's name with AriaLabelledBy.
    AriaLabel string
    // AriaLabelledBy is the element that names the slider.
    AriaLabelledBy tela.ElementRef
}
```

ColorSliderOptions configures [`UseColorSlider`](#func-usecolorslider): a slider for one channel of the shared color.

### type ColorSliderResult

```go
type ColorSliderResult struct {
    // Props go to the slider's root element: the "group" role and its
    // name.
    Props tela.Prop
    // TrackProps go to the track, which is the gradient: a press on it
    // moves the thumb to the point and starts dragging it.
    TrackProps tela.Prop
    // ThumbProps go to the thumb: the "slider" role, aria-valuenow,
    // aria-valuetext (the channel's name and value), a tab stop and the
    // handlers of [UseSlider] (arrows by one step, Shift and the page keys
    // by a page, Home and End to the ends).
    ThumbProps tela.Prop
    // TrackRef and ThumbRef are the refs that the props attach.
    TrackRef, ThumbRef tela.ElementRef
    // Channel is the channel of the slider, and Min, Max and Step its
    // range: 0 to 360 for the hue, 0 to 1 by 0.01 for the alpha and 0 to
    // 100 for the others.
    Channel        ColorChannel
    Min, Max, Step float64
    // Dragging is whether the thumb is being dragged, as of this build.
    Dragging bool
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

ColorSliderResult is what [`UseColorSlider`](#func-usecolorslider) returns.

#### func UseColorSlider

```go
func UseColorSlider(o ColorSliderOptions) ColorSliderResult
```

UseColorSlider holds the interaction of a slider for one channel of a color (React Aria's useColorSlider). It is built on [`UseSlider`](#func-useslider), so it drags, rounds and answers keys like it, with the channel's range, step and page. The caller renders the track (a gradient of TrackColors) and the thumb:

```go
st := aria.UseColorState(aria.ColorStateOptions{DefaultValue: new(tela.Hex("#6366f1"))})
hue := aria.UseColorSlider(aria.ColorSliderOptions{State: st, Channel: aria.ColorHue})
track := tela.UseSize(hue.TrackRef)
return Div(hue.Props, Class("w-64"),
    Div(hue.TrackProps, Class("relative h-3 rounded-full"),
        Div(hue.ThumbProps, Class("absolute -top-1 -ml-2.5 size-5 rounded-full border-2 border-white"),
            Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (x, y float32) {
                return float32(hue.ThumbPercent()) / 100 * track.Get().Width, 0
            })))))
```

Dragging repaints and does not build, as the slider does.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    st := aria.UseColorState(aria.ColorStateOptions{DefaultValue: new(aria.HSB{H: 220, S: 80, B: 90, A: 1}.Color())})
    hue := aria.UseColorSlider(aria.ColorSliderOptions{State: st, Channel: aria.ColorHue})
    track := tela.UseSize(hue.TrackRef)
    return Div(hue.Props, Class("w-64 p-4"),
        Div(hue.TrackProps, Class("relative h-3 w-full rounded-full bg-muted"),
            Div(hue.ThumbProps, Class("absolute -top-1 -ml-2.5 size-5 rounded-full border-2 border-white"),
                Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (x, y float32) {
                    return float32(hue.ThumbPercent()) / 100 * track.Get().Width, 0
                })))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
thumb := telatest.ByRole("slider", "Hue")
app.Focus(thumb)
app.Press("PageUp") // a page of hue is 15 degrees
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Expect(thumb, telatest.HasValue("Hue 235°"))
// Output:
// - group "Hue":
//   - slider "Hue"
```

#### func (ColorSliderResult) ThumbPercent

```go
func (r ColorSliderResult) ThumbPercent() float64
```

ThumbPercent returns the position of the thumb along the track as it is now, from 0 (Min) to 100 (Max), exactly as [`SliderResult.ThumbPercent`](#func-sliderresult-thumbpercent): it subscribes what reads it, so read it in a paint-phase closure to place the thumb while it is dragged without building the component.

#### func (ColorSliderResult) TrackColors

```go
func (r ColorSliderResult) TrackColors() []tela.Color
```

TrackColors returns the colors of the track from the minimum of the channel to its maximum, with the other channels of the color as they are now: the stops of the gradient behind the thumb. The hue has seven (every 60 degrees), the lightness three (black, the color, white) and the other channels two. For the alpha the first is transparent and the last opaque, to show over a checkerboard. It subscribes what reads it, so a track whose gradient follows the color is drawn from a paint-phase closure.

#### func (ColorSliderResult) Value

```go
func (r ColorSliderResult) Value() float64
```

Value returns the value of the channel as it is now, in the channel's range. Like ThumbPercent it subscribes what reads it.

#### func (ColorSliderResult) ValueText

```go
func (r ColorSliderResult) ValueText() string
```

ValueText returns the text of the value as it is now.

### type ColorState

```go
type ColorState struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

ColorState is the color that the area, the sliders and the field of one picker share (react-stately's useColorPickerState), made by [`UseColorState`](#func-usecolorstate). It keeps the color as an [`HSB`](#type-hsb) and not as the [`tela.Color`](API-Reference-tela#type-color) it reports, so that dragging through a gray or through black does not lose the hue (or the saturation), and a color the caller passes back is recognized as the one the state reported.

The hooks that use a ColorState must be called in the component that made it: the state asks that component to build when a drag starts, when it ends and when the pointer has rested, as the slider does, and not on every move.

#### func UseColorState

```go
func UseColorState(o ColorStateOptions) *ColorState
```

UseColorState holds the color of a picker and returns the state that [`UseColorArea`](#func-usecolorarea), [`UseColorSlider`](#func-usecolorslider) and [`UseColorField`](#func-usecolorfield) share.

#### func (*ColorState) Color

```go
func (s *ColorState) Color() tela.Color
```

Color returns the color as of the last build. While a drag moves an uncontrolled state the build waits for the pointer to rest or the drag to end; read [`ColorState.LiveColor`](#func-colorstate-livecolor) in a paint-phase closure for the color that is shown now.

#### func (*ColorState) HSB

```go
func (s *ColorState) HSB() HSB
```

HSB returns the color as of the last build, in the HSB model with the hue it keeps.

#### func (*ColorState) LiveColor

```go
func (s *ColorState) LiveColor() tela.Color
```

LiveColor returns the color as it is now. It subscribes what reads it: read it in a paint-phase closure (tela.BgFn, tela.TextColorFn) to follow a drag without building; read in the component's body it makes the component build on every move.

#### func (*ColorState) LiveHSB

```go
func (s *ColorState) LiveHSB() HSB
```

LiveHSB is [`ColorState.LiveColor`](#func-colorstate-livecolor) in the HSB model.

#### func (*ColorState) Set

```go
func (s *ColorState) Set(c tela.Color)
```

Set asks for a color, as a swatch or a hex field does. A color that is the one the state holds changes nothing; a gray keeps the hue.

#### func (*ColorState) SetHSB

```go
func (s *ColorState) SetHSB(h HSB)
```

SetHSB asks for a color in the HSB model. The values are clamped to their ranges.

### type ColorStateOptions

```go
type ColorStateOptions struct {
    // Value points to the color of a controlled state; nil leaves it to
    // the hook.
    Value *tela.Color
    // DefaultValue is the color of an uncontrolled state at the start; nil
    // starts at opaque black (tela.Black). It is a pointer because the
    // zero Color is a color too, transparent black: new(tela.Hex("#6366f1")).
    DefaultValue *tela.Color
    // OnChange is called with the next color every time the user changes
    // it: while dragging, on each key, on a hex commit and when a swatch is
    // set. The color is in the sRGB gamut.
    OnChange func(tela.Color)
}
```

ColorStateOptions configures [`UseColorState`](#func-usecolorstate).

The color is uncontrolled when Value is nil (the state keeps it, starting at DefaultValue) and controlled when Value points to the caller's state: the hooks show it and only ask OnChange for the next one, so a change the caller does not store is refused. OnChange is also called for an uncontrolled state.

```go
// A picker that keeps its color.
aria.ColorStateOptions{DefaultValue: new(tela.Hex("#6366f1"))}
// A controlled one.
c, setC := tela.UseState(tela.Hex("#6366f1"))
aria.ColorStateOptions{Value: &c, OnChange: setC.Set}
```

### type ComboboxOptions

```go
type ComboboxOptions[K comparable] struct {
    // Keys are the items to show, filtered by the caller: the caller keeps
    // the text, filters its data as it likes (a server search, a fuzzy
    // match) and gives the result on every build. Or give Items.
    Keys []K
    // Items are all the items, in order, and the hook shows the ones that
    // match the text with Filter (React Aria's defaultItems with
    // defaultFilter). Give Keys or Items, not both; an empty, non-nil Items
    // is a combobox without items. ComboboxResult.Keys are the items to
    // render.
    Items []K
    // Filter decides whether the text of an item matches what is typed;
    // [Contains] (the default), [StartsWith] or your own function. It
    // applies to Items only.
    Filter Filter
    // TextValue is the text of an item: it goes to the input when the item
    // is chosen and Filter matches it. The default is fmt.Sprint of the
    // key.
    TextValue         func(K) string
    DisabledKeys      []K
    Selected          Selection[K]
    DefaultSelected   Selection[K]
    OnSelectionChange func(Selection[K])
    // InputValue points to the text of a controlled combobox, with
    // OnInputChange asking for the next one; nil leaves it to the hook,
    // which starts at DefaultInputValue (else the text of the selected
    // item). OnInputChange is also called for an uncontrolled combobox and
    // for the text that choosing an item or leaving the input puts back.
    InputValue        *string
    DefaultInputValue string
    OnInputChange     func(string)
    // Open points to the open state of a controlled list; nil leaves it to
    // the hook, starting at DefaultOpen. OnOpenChange is called with the
    // next state.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)
    // MenuTrigger is how the list opens: [MenuTriggerInput] (the default),
    // [MenuTriggerFocus] or [MenuTriggerManual]. ArrowDown (first item)
    // and ArrowUp (last) and the toggle button open it in every mode, with
    // all the items.
    MenuTrigger string
    // AllowsCustomValue lets the text stay as typed when the input loses
    // the focus or Enter is pressed with no item chosen, clearing the
    // selection. Without it the text goes back to that of the selected item
    // (empty when none is).
    AllowsCustomValue bool
    // AllowsEmptyCollection keeps the list open when no item matches, to
    // show a "no results" message. By default it closes.
    AllowsEmptyCollection bool
    // Disabled makes the input and the button inert and disabled; ReadOnly
    // makes the input read-only and the list does not open.
    Disabled, ReadOnly bool
    // ShouldFocusWrap makes ArrowDown on the last item highlight the first,
    // and ArrowUp on the first the last.
    ShouldFocusWrap bool
    // Placement is where the popover goes around its anchor, one of
    // Floating UI's 12 placements; "bottom-start" by default. Offset is the
    // distance in pixels, and Floating are more options of [UseFloating].
    Placement string
    Offset    float32
    Floating  []FloatingOption
    // MatchWidth makes the popover as wide as the anchor.
    MatchWidth bool
    // AnchorRef is the element the popover is placed next to and
    // MatchWidth measures: the wrapper of the input and the button, say. The
    // zero value anchors it to the input.
    AnchorRef tela.ElementRef
    // AriaLabel names the input when there is no label element; with
    // LabelProps the label element names it.
    AriaLabel string
    // ButtonLabel is the accessible name of the toggle button that
    // ButtonProps go to (default "Show suggestions"). Set it to translate
    // the name.
    ButtonLabel string
    // Ref is the input's ref, for a hook used together with others on the
    // same element; the zero value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

ComboboxOptions configures [`UseCombobox`](#func-usecombobox). The items are keyed like those of a list box: see [`ListBoxOptions`](#type-listboxoptions) for TextValue, DisabledKeys, and the controlled and uncontrolled Selected, DefaultSelected and OnSelectionChange (a combobox holds at most one selected key).

### type ComboboxResult

```go
type ComboboxResult[K comparable] struct {
    // InputProps go to the Input: the "combobox" role, the text and its
    // change, the keys (arrows, Enter, Tab, Escape), aria-autocomplete,
    // aria-expanded, aria-controls while open and aria-activedescendant
    // for the highlighted item. The input keeps the focus: the items are
    // highlighted, never focused.
    InputProps tela.Prop
    // ButtonProps go to an optional toggle button: it shows or hides the
    // list with every item, and keeps the focus on the input. It is not a
    // tab stop and is labelled with ButtonLabel ("Show suggestions" by
    // default; an AriaLabel after the props also changes it).
    ButtonProps tela.Prop
    // LabelProps go to the label element: it names the input, and a click
    // on it focuses the input.
    LabelProps tela.Prop
    // PopoverProps go to the popover's element, which holds the list box:
    // it is fixed to the window and placed next to the anchor in the frame
    // that shows it, it is on the overlay stack (Escape closes it), and a
    // press in it keeps the focus on the input. With MatchWidth it is as
    // wide as the anchor. Render it in a Portal, only while Open.
    PopoverProps tela.Prop
    // ArrowProps go to an arrow element inside the popover.
    ArrowProps tela.Prop
    // ListBox is the list: its Props go to the element that holds the
    // items and ItemProps(k) to each item, as in [UseListBox]. The items
    // are rendered inside the popover, only while Open, from Keys.
    ListBox ListBoxResult[K]
    // Keys are the items to render: ComboboxOptions.Keys, or the Items that
    // match the text (all of them after the list was opened with the
    // arrows or the button, until the text changes).
    Keys []K
    // InputValue is the text of the input.
    InputValue string
    // ShowAll is true after the list was opened by hand (the button, the
    // arrows, or the focus with MenuTriggerFocus) and until the text
    // changes: the list shows every item whatever the text. A hook given
    // Items does it itself; a caller who filters Keys should too.
    ShowAll bool
    // Selected is the current selection: [Selection.First] is the selected
    // key.
    Selected Selection[K]
    // Open is whether the list is open; SetOpen asks for a state, Toggle for
    // the other one and Close for closed.
    Open    bool
    SetOpen func(open bool)
    Toggle  func()
    Close   func()
    // Pressed is true while the button is pressed.
    Pressed bool
    // Placement is the popover's placement after flipping (see
    // [PopoverResult]).
    Placement string
    // InputRef, ButtonRef and PopoverRef are the refs of those elements.
    InputRef, ButtonRef, PopoverRef tela.ElementRef
}
```

ComboboxResult is what [`UseCombobox`](#func-usecombobox) returns.

#### func UseCombobox

```go
func UseCombobox[K comparable](o ComboboxOptions[K]) ComboboxResult[K]
```

UseCombobox holds the state of a combobox and returns the props of its input, its toggle button, its popover and its list (React Aria's useComboBox with useComboBoxState): a text field that filters a list of options, and a list that opens next to it.

```go
cb := aria.UseCombobox(aria.ComboboxOptions[string]{
    Items: fruit, TextValue: capital, AriaLabel: "Fruit", MatchWidth: true,
})
return Fragment(
    Div(Class("flex"),
        Input(cb.InputProps, Class("w-48 rounded-l-md border px-3 py-2")),
        Button(cb.ButtonProps, Class("rounded-r-md border px-2"), Icon(chevronDown))),
    Portal(If(cb.Open,
        Div(cb.PopoverProps, Class("rounded-md border bg-popover p-1 shadow-md"),
            Div(cb.ListBox.Props, Class("max-h-60 overflow-auto"),
                Range(len(cb.Keys), func(i int) tela.Node {
                    k := cb.Keys[i]
                    return Div(cb.ListBox.ItemProps(k), Key(k),
                        Class("rounded px-2 py-1.5 aria-selected:font-medium"),
                        If(cb.ListBox.IsFocused(k), Class("bg-accent")), Text(capital(k)))
                }))))))
```

Typing filters the list and opens it (see MenuTrigger). The input keeps the focus: ArrowDown and ArrowUp highlight the next and previous item (the first and the last, opening the list when closed), Enter chooses the highlighted item, which sets the text to its TextValue and closes the list, Tab chooses it and moves on, and Escape closes the list and puts the text back to that of the selected item (cleared when there is none). When the input loses the focus the text is committed: reset to the selected item's, or kept as a custom value with AllowsCustomValue. Home, End, Space and the left and right arrows stay with the text field, and nothing moves while an IME composes text.

Items are highlighted with [`Collection.IsFocused`](#func-collectionk-isfocused) (there is no DOM focus on them); the input carries aria-activedescendant. In the aria snapshot the input is `combobox "Fruit" [expanded]: b`, the button `button "Show suggestions"` and the list a listbox named by the label.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    cb := aria.UseCombobox(aria.ComboboxOptions[string]{
        Items: fruits, TextValue: capital, AriaLabel: "Fruit", MatchWidth: true,
    })
    return Div(Class("p-4"),
        Div(Class("flex"),
            Input(cb.InputProps, Class("w-48 rounded-l-md border px-3 py-2")),
            Button(cb.ButtonProps, Class("rounded-r-md border px-2"), Text("v"))),
        Portal(If(cb.Open,
            Div(cb.PopoverProps, Class("rounded-md border bg-popover p-1 shadow-md"),
                Div(cb.ListBox.Props, Class("max-h-60 overflow-auto"),
                    Range(len(cb.Keys), func(i int) tela.Node {
                        k := cb.Keys[i]
                        return Div(cb.ListBox.ItemProps(k), Key(k), Class("rounded px-2 py-1.5"),
                            If(cb.ListBox.IsFocused(k), Class("bg-accent")), Text(capital(k)))
                    }))))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page, telatest.Size(400, 300))
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("combobox", "Fruit"))
app.Type("blu") // filters and opens the list
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Press("ArrowDown") // highlights the item, the input keeps the focus
app.Press("Enter")     // chooses it
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - combobox "Fruit" [expanded]: blu
// - button "Show suggestions" [expanded]: v
// - listbox "Fruit":
//   - option "Blueberry"
// - combobox "Fruit": Blueberry
// - button "Show suggestions": v
```

**Example (allowsCustomValue)**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    cb := aria.UseCombobox(aria.ComboboxOptions[string]{
        Items: fruits, TextValue: capital, AriaLabel: "Tag", AllowsCustomValue: true,
        OnSelectionChange: func(s aria.Selection[string]) { fmt.Println("selected:", s) },
    })
    return Input(cb.InputProps, Class("w-48 border"))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page, telatest.Size(300, 100))
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("combobox", "Tag"))
app.Fill(telatest.ByRole("combobox", "Tag"), "kiwi")
app.Press("Tab") // the text stays, and the selection is cleared
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output: - combobox "Tag": kiwi
```

### type ContextMenuTriggerOptions

```go
type ContextMenuTriggerOptions struct {
    // Open points to the open state of a controlled menu; nil leaves the
    // state to the hook, which starts closed. OnOpenChange is called with
    // the next state: for a controlled menu it is how the change is asked
    // for, for an uncontrolled one a notification. A menu opens at a point,
    // so there is no DefaultOpen.
    Open         *bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)
    // Disabled makes the area ignore the gestures that open the menu: the
    // browser's (here, the platform's) own, and an outer context menu's,
    // take over.
    Disabled bool
    // NoLongPress keeps a touch that stays down from opening the menu. The
    // long press is recognized for every pointer of the area, so a mouse
    // button held for 500 ms on the area, or on a child that is not itself
    // a long-press target, does not click; turn it off for an area whose
    // content is used that way.
    NoLongPress bool
    // Ref is the area's ref and MenuRef the menu's, for hooks used together
    // with others on the same element; the zero value makes the hook
    // create its own.
    Ref, MenuRef tela.ElementRef
}
```

ContextMenuTriggerOptions configures [`UseContextMenuTrigger`](#func-usecontextmenutrigger).

### type ContextMenuTriggerResult

```go
type ContextMenuTriggerResult struct {
    // TriggerProps go to the area that has the context menu: the ref and
    // the gestures that open the menu (see [UseContextMenuTrigger]).
    TriggerProps tela.Prop
    // MenuProps go to the menu's element: the ref and a focus scope that
    // gives the focus back when the menu closes. The menu's other hooks and
    // [UsePopover] share MenuRef. The menu has no name of its own: give
    // [MenuOptions].AriaLabel one.
    MenuProps tela.Prop
    // Open is whether the menu is open.
    Open bool
    // FocusStrategy is where the focus goes when the menu opens:
    // [FocusFirst] for a key or a long press, "" for the menu itself
    // (opened with a mouse). Pass it to [MenuOptions].FocusStrategy.
    FocusStrategy string
    // Anchor returns the virtual rectangle the menu is placed at, in window
    // coordinates: a point where the pointer was or the area's top-left
    // corner. It is [AnchorRect]'s argument, for a menu placed with
    // [UseFloating] instead of [UsePopover].
    Anchor func() tela.Rect
    // OpenAt opens the menu at a point of the window (a click handler of
    // your own, a "More" button). Close closes it, and a menu closes itself
    // when an item is chosen by calling Close. SetOpen asks for a state.
    OpenAt  func(x, y float32)
    SetOpen func(open bool)
    Close   func()
    // Ref is the area's ref and MenuRef the menu's.
    Ref, MenuRef tela.ElementRef
}
```

ContextMenuTriggerResult is what [`UseContextMenuTrigger`](#func-usecontextmenutrigger) returns.

#### func UseContextMenuTrigger

```go
func UseContextMenuTrigger(o ContextMenuTriggerOptions) ContextMenuTriggerResult
```

UseContextMenuTrigger holds the open state of a context menu and returns the props of its area, which opens the menu at the pointer (the contextmenu event of the platform, Radix UI's ContextMenu):

- a right click, at the pointer (the focus stays where it was, and the menu itself takes it),
- a touch that stays down for 500 ms (h.OnLongPress), at the finger, with the first item focused,
- Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key, with the first item focused, at the top-left corner of the area.

The event's default is prevented and its propagation stopped, so the innermost area with a context menu wins. The menu is rendered by the caller, in a Portal, and [`UsePopover`](#func-usepopover) places it at the point with [`AnchorRect`](#func-anchorrect), flipped and shifted to stay in the window; Escape, a primary press outside, the focus leaving and choosing an item close it, and the focus goes back to where it was. A right click on the area while the menu is open moves it to the new point; one outside the area does nothing (the overlay stack only dismisses for primary presses).

```go
cm := aria.UseContextMenuTrigger(aria.ContextMenuTriggerOptions{})
return Fragment(
    Div(cm.TriggerProps, Class("h-48 w-full rounded-md border"), Text("Right click here")),
    Portal(If(cm.Open, fileMenu{cm})))

type fileMenu struct{ cm aria.ContextMenuTriggerResult }

func (m fileMenu) Build() tela.Node {
    pop := aria.UsePopover(m.cm.PopoverOptions())
    menu := aria.UseMenu(aria.MenuOptions[string]{
        Keys: actions, OnAction: run, OnClose: m.cm.Close, AriaLabel: "Actions",
        AutoFocus: true, FocusStrategy: m.cm.FocusStrategy, Ref: m.cm.MenuRef,
    })
    return Div(pop.Props, m.cm.MenuProps, menu.Props, Class("w-48 rounded-md border bg-popover p-1"), ...)
}
```

The menu is the one of a dropdown menu: [`UseMenu`](#func-usemenu) takes the same results. The area is not focusable by itself; the keys reach it from the element inside it that has the focus, and a keyboard menu opens at the area's corner, not at that element.

**Example**

```go
// A context menu: Shift+F10 on the focused button opens it, Enter
// chooses the first item and the focus goes back to the button.
var ev events
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, ctxPage(aria.ContextMenuTriggerOptions{}, &ev), telatest.Size(400, 300))
app.Focus(telatest.ByTestID("inner"))
app.Press("Shift+F10")
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Press("Enter")
app.ExpectFocused(telatest.ByTestID("inner"))
fmt.Println(ev.take())
// Output:
// - button "Inner"
// - button "Outside"
// - menu "Actions":
//   - menuitem "Copy"
//   - menuitem "Paste"
//   - menuitem "Delete"
// action:copy
```

#### func (ContextMenuTriggerResult) PopoverOptions

```go
func (r ContextMenuTriggerResult) PopoverOptions() PopoverOptions
```

PopoverOptions returns the options of [`UsePopover`](#func-usepopover) for the menu: anchored at the point the menu was opened with ("bottom-start", flipped and shifted to stay in the window). The popover is not modal, so that a right click on the area while the menu is open reaches it and moves the menu to the new point; a primary press outside the menu closes it. Change what you need in the value returned (Offset, Floating).

### type Date

```go
type Date struct {
    Year  int
    Month time.Month
    Day   int
}
```

Date is a day of the Gregorian calendar, without a time of day or a time zone: what a calendar selects ("the 5th of October 2026"), the same wherever it is read. The zero Date means "no date".

It is a comparable value, unlike a time.Time (whose == also compares the zone pointer and the monotonic clock), so it can be a map key, the state of tela.UseState, a prop that skips a build when it is equal, and it has no daylight saving time to trip date arithmetic on: AddDays(1) is always the next day. Convert with [`DateOf`](#func-dateof) and [`Date.Time`](#func-date-time).

```go
d := aria.Date{Year: 2026, Month: time.October, Day: 5}
d.AddMonths(1)            // 2026-11-05
d.AddDays(-5)             // 2026-09-30
aria.Date{2026, 1, 31}.AddMonths(1) // 2026-02-28: the day is clamped
```

**Example**

```go
oct := aria.Date{Year: 2026, Month: time.October, Day: 31}
fmt.Println(oct.AddMonths(1), oct.AddDays(1), oct.Weekday())
fmt.Println(aria.DateOf(time.Date(2026, 1, 31, 23, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)).AddMonths(1))
// Output:
// 2026-11-30 2026-11-01 Saturday
// 2026-02-28
```

#### func DateOf

```go
func DateOf(t time.Time) Date
```

DateOf returns the calendar day of t in t's own time zone.

#### func Today

```go
func Today() Date
```

Today returns the current day in the local time zone. Calendars take their notion of today from an option (CalendarOptions.Today), so tests can fix it; this is the default.

#### func (Date) AddDays

```go
func (d Date) AddDays(n int) Date
```

AddDays returns the day n days after d (before it when n is negative).

#### func (Date) AddMonths

```go
func (d Date) AddMonths(n int) Date
```

AddMonths returns the same day of the month n months after d; when that month is shorter the day is the last one of it (January 31 plus one month is February 28 or 29).

#### func (Date) AddYears

```go
func (d Date) AddYears(n int) Date
```

AddYears returns the same day n years after d, with the day clamped like [`Date.AddMonths`](#func-date-addmonths) (February 29 plus one year is February 28).

#### func (Date) After

```go
func (d Date) After(o Date) bool
```

After reports whether d is a day after o.

#### func (Date) Before

```go
func (d Date) Before(o Date) bool
```

Before reports whether d is a day before o.

#### func (Date) Compare

```go
func (d Date) Compare(o Date) int
```

Compare returns -1, 0 or 1 when d is before, the same as or after o.

#### func (Date) IsValid

```go
func (d Date) IsValid() bool
```

IsValid reports whether d is a day that exists: January 1 of year 1 to December 31 of year 9999, with the right number of days in its month.

#### func (Date) IsZero

```go
func (d Date) IsZero() bool
```

IsZero reports whether d is the zero Date, no date at all.

#### func (Date) String

```go
func (d Date) String() string
```

String returns d as ISO 8601, "2026-10-05" (and "none" for the zero Date). Unlike a localized date it is unique per day, so it is the key of a calendar cell: Key(day.String()).

#### func (Date) Time

```go
func (d Date) Time(loc *time.Location) time.Time
```

Time returns midnight of d in loc (UTC when loc is nil).

#### func (Date) Weekday

```go
func (d Date) Weekday() time.Weekday
```

Weekday returns the day of the week of d.

### type DateRange

```go
type DateRange struct {
    Start, End Date
}
```

DateRange is a span of days, both ends included: the value of a range calendar. It is the zero value when nothing is selected; Start is never after End in a range a calendar makes.

#### func (DateRange) Contains

```go
func (r DateRange) Contains(d Date) bool
```

Contains reports whether d is in r, its ends included.

#### func (DateRange) IsZero

```go
func (r DateRange) IsZero() bool
```

IsZero reports whether r is the empty selection.

### type DialogOptions

```go
type DialogOptions struct {
    // Role is "dialog" (the default) or "alertdialog", for a dialog that
    // interrupts the user with a message that needs a response. Another
    // value panics in dev mode.
    Role string
    // Modal marks the dialog aria-modal and keeps Tab inside it. Make the
    // dialog's [UseOverlay] modal too, so that the rest of the window is
    // inert.
    Modal bool
    // AriaLabel names the dialog when it has no visible title. Without it
    // the dialog is named by the element that has TitleProps.
    AriaLabel string
    // Ref is the dialog element's ref, for a hook used together with others
    // on the same element (the overlay trigger's OverlayRef, UsePopover);
    // the zero value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

DialogOptions configures [`UseDialog`](#func-usedialog).

### type DialogResult

```go
type DialogResult struct {
    // Props go to the dialog's element: its role, aria-modal, its name, a
    // focus scope that moves the focus into the dialog when it opens, keeps
    // it there (with Modal) and gives it back to the element that had it
    // when the dialog closes, and the ref.
    Props tela.Prop
    // TitleProps go to the element that titles the dialog (a heading): its
    // text names the dialog.
    TitleProps tela.Prop
    // Manager moves the focus inside the dialog.
    Manager FocusManager
    // Ref is the ref attached to the dialog's element by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

DialogResult is what [`UseDialog`](#func-usedialog) returns.

#### func UseDialog

```go
func UseDialog(o DialogOptions) DialogResult
```

UseDialog returns the props of a dialog (React Aria's useDialog): its role, its name from the title, and the focus: it goes to the first tabbable element inside when the dialog opens (the dialog itself when there is none), and returns to the element that had it when the dialog closes. Combine it with [`UseOverlay`](#func-useoverlay) for the dismissal and the modality, on the same element.

```go
dlg := aria.UseDialog(aria.DialogOptions{Modal: true})
ov := aria.UseOverlay(aria.OverlayOptions{Open: open, OnClose: close, Dismissable: true, Modal: true})
return Portal(If(open,
    Div(ov.Props, dlg.Props, Class("w-96 rounded-xl bg-background p-6 shadow-xl"),
        H2(dlg.TitleProps, Class("text-lg font-semibold"), Text("Delete project?")),
        Button(OnClick(close), Text("Cancel")))))
```

An "alertdialog" is not dismissed by a press outside it: leave Dismissable off. The dialog element takes the focus when it has nothing tabbable (it is focusable with a script, not in the Tab order), and, in a modal dialog, when the focused element inside it unmounts (Radix's FocusScope), so the keys still reach the dialog and Tab goes on inside.

**Example**

```go
// A modal dialog named by its title: it takes the focus when it opens,
// keeps Tab inside, and gives the focus back when it closes.
page := func() tela.Node {
    trig := aria.UseOverlayTrigger(aria.OverlayTriggerOptions{})
    ov := aria.UseOverlay(aria.OverlayOptions{Open: trig.Open, OnClose: trig.Close, Dismissable: true, Modal: true})
    dlg := aria.UseDialog(aria.DialogOptions{Modal: true, Ref: trig.OverlayRef})
    return Div(
        Button(trig.TriggerProps, Text("Delete")),
        Portal(If(trig.Open,
            Div(ov.Props, dlg.Props, Class("w-64 bg-white p-4"),
                H2(dlg.TitleProps, Text("Delete project?")),
                Button(Text("Cancel")),
                Button(OnClick(trig.Close), Text("Delete"))))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(300, 200))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Delete"))
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Press("Escape")
app.ExpectFocused(telatest.ByRole("button", "Delete"))
// Output:
// - dialog "Delete project?":
//   - heading "Delete project?" [level=2]
//   - button "Cancel"
//   - button "Delete"
```

### type Filter

```go
type Filter func(text, query string) bool
```

Filter decides whether the text of an item matches what the user typed: the filter of [`ComboboxOptions`](#type-comboboxoptions). Contains, StartsWith and EndsWith are ready to use.

### type FlipOptions

```go
type FlipOptions struct {
    // Padding is the space to keep between the element and the edges of the
    // area it must stay in (the window, or the visible part of the scroll
    // containers around it when it is not in a Portal).
    Padding float32
    // NoMainAxis stops flip from checking the overflow on the side of the
    // placement (Floating UI's mainAxis: false); NoCrossAxis on the
    // alignment axis (crossAxis: false).
    NoMainAxis, NoCrossAxis bool
    // CrossAxisAlignment is Floating UI's crossAxis: 'alignment': the
    // overflow on the alignment axis only counts while the next placement
    // is on the same axis as the initial one, so the element changes side
    // only when every placement on its side overflows.
    CrossAxisAlignment bool
    // FallbackPlacements are the placements to try, in order, after the
    // initial one. Nil tries the opposite one (and, for an aligned
    // placement, its other alignments first).
    FallbackPlacements []string
    // FallbackStrategy is what to do when no placement fits: "bestFit" (the
    // default) takes the one that overflows least, "initialPlacement" goes
    // back to the initial one.
    FallbackStrategy string
    // FallbackAxisSideDirection adds the placements on the other axis to
    // the fallbacks when FallbackPlacements is nil: "none" (the default),
    // "start" or "end", the side tried first.
    FallbackAxisSideDirection string
    // NoFlipAlignment stops an aligned placement from trying its other
    // alignment (Floating UI's flipAlignment: false).
    NoFlipAlignment bool
}
```

FlipOptions are the options of [`Flip`](#func-flip); the zero value is Floating UI's defaults.

### type Floating

```go
type Floating struct {
    // Props go on the floating element: they make it fixed to the window at
    // its top-left corner (a later class such as "absolute" in the element's
    // Class wins) and place it next to its anchor. Put the element in a
    // Portal so that no ancestor clips it.
    Props tela.Prop
    // ArrowProps go on the arrow element (the one whose ElementRef was given
    // to [Arrow]): they make it absolute at the top-left corner of its
    // parent, the floating element, and move it so that it points at the
    // anchor, half of it outside the floating element's border box on the
    // side that faces the anchor. Without the [Arrow] middleware they do
    // nothing but make it absolute.
    ArrowProps tela.Prop
    // Placement is the placement the floating element is in, after flip or
    // autoPlacement chose it: one of Floating UI's 12 placements. It is the
    // placement given to [Placement] (default "bottom") until the first
    // position is computed, and is the engine's in the frame that shows the
    // element (the build that read the first one runs again before the frame
    // is painted): use it to style.
    Placement string
    // Side and Align split Placement: Side is "top", "right", "bottom" or
    // "left", the side of the anchor the element is on; Align is "start",
    // "end" or "" (centered).
    Side, Align string
    // ArrowX and ArrowY are Floating UI's arrow data: the offset of the
    // arrow along the floating element's edge that faces the anchor, from the
    // element's left edge (ArrowX, for the top and bottom sides) or top edge
    // (ArrowY, for left and right); the other one is 0. They are valid in the
    // frame where they change: read them in a paint-phase closure such as
    // tela.TranslateFn. Zero without the [Arrow] middleware.
    ArrowX, ArrowY *tela.Value[float32]
    // ReferenceHidden reports that the anchor is scrolled out of view (the
    // [Hide] middleware, strategy "referenceHidden"); Escaped that the
    // floating element is out of the area where the anchor can be seen
    // (strategy "escaped"). They are false without [Hide], and an anchor that
    // is not displayed counts as hidden. Read them in a paint-phase closure
    // to follow the same frame:
    //
    //	Style(tela.OpacityFn(tela.MapValue(fl.ReferenceHidden, func(hidden bool) float32 {
    //	    if hidden { return 0 }
    //	    return 1
    //	})))
    ReferenceHidden, Escaped *tela.Value[bool]
}
```

Floating is what [`UseFloating`](#func-usefloating) returns: the props of the floating element and of its arrow, and what the position computed.

Everything the position decides is known in the frame that shows the element: Props and ArrowProps move it and the arrow while the frame is painted, so no frame ever shows them in the wrong place. A component that styles itself by Placement builds again in that same frame, before anything is shown, when the placement differs from the one it built with (a flip), and what mounted in the frame starts its transitions again from its starting style: a menu that flips above its trigger enters from the top side's classes in its first frame (ADR-164).

#### func UseFloating

```go
func UseFloating(anchor tela.ElementRef, opts ...FloatingOption) Floating
```

UseFloating positions a floating element (a popover, tooltip, menu or select list) next to its anchor: Floating UI's computePosition with its middleware, run by Tela's frame pipeline (ADR-099). It is a hook: call it at the top level of a component.

```go
func Popover(open bool) tela.Node {
    anchor := tela.UseElementRef()
    arrow := tela.UseElementRef()
    fl := aria.UseFloating(anchor, aria.Placement("bottom-start"), aria.Offset(8),
        aria.Flip(), aria.Shift(8), aria.Arrow(arrow))
    return Fragment(
        Button(Ref(anchor), Text("Open")),
        If(open, Portal(
            Div(fl.Props, Class("w-64 rounded-md border bg-popover p-4 shadow-md"),
                Text("Content"),
                Div(Ref(arrow), fl.ArrowProps, Class("size-2 rotate-45 border bg-popover"))))))
}
```

The anchor is the element that carries the ref (h.Ref), or, when anchor is the zero tela.ElementRef, the virtual rectangle that [`AnchorRect`](#func-anchorrect) returns, such as the pointer of a context menu. The options configure the placement and the middleware, which run in the order given, as in Floating UI's middleware array, and the order matters: offset before flip and shift, arrow last.

The element is placed in the paint phase of the frame that shows it, on the anchor as painted: it follows its anchor when an ancestor scrolls or a transform moves it, without a frame of its own, and nothing runs while nothing changes. The options are read again on every build of the component.

**Example**

```go
// A menu below its button, offset by 4 px, flipped above it when the
// window has no room below and kept 8 px from the window's edges.
menu := func() tela.Node {
    anchor := tela.UseElementRef()
    fl := aria.UseFloating(anchor,
        aria.Placement("bottom-start"), aria.Offset(4), aria.Flip(), aria.Shift(8))
    return Div(Class("relative h-full"),
        Button(Ref(anchor), TestID("button"), Class("absolute left-4 top-[260px] h-8 w-24"), Text("Menu")),
        Portal(Div(fl.Props, TestID("menu"), Class("h-24 w-48 rounded-md border bg-white"),
            Textf("placement: %s", fl.Placement))))
}
app := telatest.Mount(&exampleTB{}, tela.C(menu), telatest.Size(400, 300))

button := app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("button"))
pop := app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("menu"))
fmt.Printf("button y %.0f to %.0f\n", button.Y, button.Bottom())
fmt.Printf("menu y %.0f to %.0f, above the button\n", pop.Y, pop.Bottom())
app.ExpectText("placement: top-start")
// Output:
// button y 260 to 292
// menu y 160 to 256, above the button
```

### type FloatingOption

```go
type FloatingOption struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

FloatingOption configures [`UseFloating`](#func-usefloating): the placement, a virtual anchor or a middleware. Build them with [`Placement`](#func-placement), [`AnchorRect`](#func-anchorrect), [`Offset`](#func-offset), [`Flip`](#func-flip), [`Shift`](#func-shift), [`Size`](#func-size), [`Arrow`](#func-arrow), [`Hide`](#func-hide) and [`AutoPlacement`](#func-autoplacement).

#### func AnchorRect

```go
func AnchorRect(rect func() tela.Rect) FloatingOption
```

AnchorRect makes the anchor a virtual rectangle (Floating UI's virtual elements), for a context menu at the pointer or a popover at a text selection. rect returns it in window coordinates (for the pointer, a Rect of zero size at its position). It runs in the paint phase of the frames that place the element; a tela.Value it reads with Get places the element again when the value changes. It is used when the anchor given to [`UseFloating`](#func-usefloating) is the zero tela.ElementRef:

```go
pos := tela.UseValue(tela.Rect{})
fl := aria.UseFloating(tela.ElementRef{}, aria.Placement("bottom-start"), aria.Flip(),
    aria.AnchorRect(pos.Get))
```

**Example**

```go
// A context menu at the pointer: a virtual anchor, the zero ElementRef.
var pointer *tela.Value[tela.Rect]
menu := func() tela.Node {
    pointer = tela.UseValue(tela.Rect{X: 120, Y: 80})
    fl := aria.UseFloating(tela.ElementRef{},
        aria.Placement("bottom-start"), aria.Flip(), aria.Shift(4),
        aria.AnchorRect(pointer.Get))
    return Div(Class("h-full"),
        Portal(Div(fl.Props, TestID("menu"), Class("h-24 w-40 rounded-md bg-white"))))
}
app := telatest.Mount(&exampleTB{}, tela.C(menu), telatest.Size(400, 300))

r := app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("menu"))
fmt.Printf("at the pointer: x %.0f y %.0f\n", r.X, r.Y)

pointer.Set(tela.Rect{X: 200, Y: 40})
app.WaitFor("the menu to follow the pointer", func() bool {
    return app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("menu")).X == 200
})
r = app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("menu"))
fmt.Printf("moved: x %.0f y %.0f\n", r.X, r.Y)
// Output:
// at the pointer: x 120 y 80
// moved: x 200 y 40
```

#### func Arrow

```go
func Arrow(ref tela.ElementRef, opts ...ArrowOptions) FloatingOption
```

Arrow computes where the arrow element points at the anchor (Floating UI's arrow). ref is the ref of the arrow element, attached with h.Ref next to the Floating's ArrowProps. Give it last, after Flip and Shift.

**Example**

```go
// An arrow that points at the button even though the popover shifted to
// stay inside the window.
tip := func() tela.Node {
    anchor, arrow := tela.UseElementRef(), tela.UseElementRef()
    fl := aria.UseFloating(anchor, aria.Offset(8), aria.Flip(), aria.Shift(8), aria.Arrow(arrow))
    return Div(Class("relative h-full"),
        Button(Ref(anchor), TestID("button"), Class("absolute left-[340px] top-10 h-8 w-10"), Text("?")),
        Portal(Div(fl.Props, TestID("tip"), Class("h-16 w-48 rounded-md bg-slate-800"),
            Div(Ref(arrow), TestID("arrow"), fl.ArrowProps, Class("size-4 rotate-45 bg-slate-800")))))
}
app := telatest.Mount(&exampleTB{}, tela.C(tip), telatest.Size(400, 300))

button := app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("button"))
arrow := app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("arrow"))
fmt.Printf("button center x %.0f\n", button.X+button.Width/2)
fmt.Printf("arrow center x %.0f\n", arrow.X+arrow.Width/2)
// Output:
// button center x 360
// arrow center x 360
```

#### func AutoPlacement

```go
func AutoPlacement(opts ...AutoPlacementOptions) FloatingOption
```

AutoPlacement chooses the placement with the most room, without a preferred one (Floating UI's autoPlacement). It is an alternative to [`Flip`](#func-flip): do not give both.

#### func Flip

```go
func Flip(opts ...FlipOptions) FloatingOption
```

Flip flips the element to the opposite side when its placement would overflow the area it must stay in (Floating UI's flip): a popover below a button near the bottom of the window goes above it. It checks the placements in order and keeps the first that fits. Give it after [`Offset`](#func-offset) and before [`Shift`](#func-shift).

#### func Hide

```go
func Hide(opts ...HideOptions) FloatingOption
```

Hide tracks whether the anchor is scrolled out of view (Floating UI's hide), published as [`Floating`](#type-floating).ReferenceHidden and [`Floating`](#type-floating).Escaped.

#### func Offset

```go
func Offset(mainAxis float32, opts ...OffsetOptions) FloatingOption
```

Offset moves the element mainAxis pixels away from the anchor, along the side it is on (Floating UI's offset): the gap between a popover and its button. Give it before [`Flip`](#func-flip) and [`Shift`](#func-shift) so that they see the final distance. The options skid it along the anchor's edge.

#### func Placement

```go
func Placement(placement string) FloatingOption
```

Placement sets the placement the floating element goes in, one of Floating UI's 12: "top", "top-start", "top-end", "right", "right-start", "right-end", "bottom" (the default), "bottom-start", "bottom-end", "left", "left-start" and "left-end". The side is where the element goes relative to the anchor; "start" and "end" align it with that edge of the anchor, mirrored in a right-to-left element (h.Dir("rtl")), as in Floating UI. An unknown placement panics in dev mode, with the closest valid one, and is ignored otherwise.

#### func Shift

```go
func Shift(padding float32, opts ...ShiftOptions) FloatingOption
```

Shift keeps the element in view by sliding it along the anchor's edge when it overflows the window (Floating UI's shift), padding pixels from the edges. It does not change the side: give it after [`Flip`](#func-flip).

#### func Size

```go
func Size(apply func(Available), opts ...SizeOptions) FloatingOption
```

Size gives apply the room the floating element has (Floating UI's size), so that a long list scrolls inside the window instead of leaving it. apply calls the methods of its argument to limit the element; the limits are applied in the same frame, with no flash of the unlimited element:

```go
aria.Size(func(a aria.Available) {
    a.MaxHeight(a.Height)
})
```

Put the element's scrolling content in an element with a bounded height (a flex column with min-h-0 and overflow-y-auto), or give the floating element itself overflow-y-auto. apply runs in the paint phase: it must be quick and must not set state. A limit that apply does not ask for in a run is removed.

**Example**

```go
// A long list limited to the room below its button: the popover is as
// tall as the window allows, 8 px from the bottom, and scrolls.
list := func() tela.Node {
    anchor := tela.UseElementRef()
    fl := aria.UseFloating(anchor, aria.Placement("bottom-start"), aria.Offset(4),
        aria.Size(func(a aria.Available) {
            a.MaxHeight(a.Height)
        }, aria.SizeOptions{Padding: 8}))
    return Div(Class("relative h-full"),
        Button(Ref(anchor), Class("absolute left-4 top-[50px] h-8 w-24"), Text("Open")),
        Portal(Div(fl.Props, TestID("list"), Class("flex w-40 flex-col overflow-y-auto bg-white"),
            Range(40, func(i int) tela.Node {
                return Div(Class("h-8 shrink-0"), Textf("Item %d", i))
            }))))
}
app := telatest.Mount(&exampleTB{}, tela.C(list), telatest.Size(400, 300))

r := app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("list"))
fmt.Printf("list y %.0f to %.0f of 300\n", r.Y, r.Bottom())
// Output:
// list y 86 to 292 of 300
```

### type FocusManager

```go
type FocusManager struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

FocusManager moves the focus among the focusable elements of a scope (React Aria's FocusManager), in tree order. Hidden, disabled and inert elements, and those outside an open modal, are not candidates. Call its methods from event handlers and effects; each reports whether it found an element to focus. The zero FocusManager does nothing.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
toolbar := func() tela.Node {
    scope := aria.UseFocusScope(aria.FocusScopeOptions{})
    return Div(scope.Props, Role("toolbar"), AriaLabel("Format"),
        OnKeyDown(func(e tela.KeyboardEvent) {
            switch e.Key {
            case tela.KeyArrowRight:
                e.PreventDefault()
                scope.Manager.FocusNext(aria.FocusOptions{Wrap: true})
            case tela.KeyArrowLeft:
                e.PreventDefault()
                scope.Manager.FocusPrevious(aria.FocusOptions{Wrap: true})
            }
        }),
        Button(Text("Bold")), Button(Text("Italic")), Button(Text("Underline")))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, toolbar)
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("button", "Underline"))
app.Press("ArrowRight") // wraps around
app.ExpectFocused(telatest.ByRole("button", "Bold"))
app.Press("ArrowLeft")
app.ExpectFocused(telatest.ByRole("button", "Underline"))
fmt.Println("the arrows move the focus")
// Output: the arrows move the focus
```

#### func (FocusManager) FocusFirst

```go
func (m FocusManager) FocusFirst(o FocusOptions) bool
```

FocusFirst focuses the first element of the scope.

#### func (FocusManager) FocusLast

```go
func (m FocusManager) FocusLast(o FocusOptions) bool
```

FocusLast focuses the last element of the scope.

#### func (FocusManager) FocusNext

```go
func (m FocusManager) FocusNext(o FocusOptions) bool
```

FocusNext focuses the element after o.From (or after the focused element) in the scope.

#### func (FocusManager) FocusPrevious

```go
func (m FocusManager) FocusPrevious(o FocusOptions) bool
```

FocusPrevious focuses the element before o.From (or before the focused element) in the scope.

### type FocusOptions

```go
type FocusOptions struct {
    // Tabbable limits the candidates to the elements in the sequential
    // focus order (h.TabIndex of 0 or more, Buttons and fields), leaving
    // out those that only a script can focus (h.TabIndex(-1)).
    Tabbable bool
    // Wrap goes around at the ends: FocusNext from the last candidate
    // focuses the first, FocusPrevious from the first focuses the last.
    // It applies to FocusNext and FocusPrevious.
    Wrap bool
    // From is where FocusNext and FocusPrevious start, an element of the
    // scope; the zero value starts from the focused element.
    From tela.ElementRef
}
```

FocusOptions configures the moves of a [`FocusManager`](#type-focusmanager).

### type FocusRingOptions

```go
type FocusRingOptions struct {
    // Within makes the ring follow the focus anywhere inside the element,
    // not only on the element itself (CSS's :focus-within and
    // React Aria's within): a group that shows a ring around all its
    // parts.
    Within bool
    // Ref is the element's ref, for a hook that is used together with
    // others on one element (see the package documentation); the zero
    // value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

FocusRingOptions configures [`UseFocusRing`](#func-usefocusring).

### type FocusRingResult

```go
type FocusRingResult struct {
    // Props go to the element: the focus, blur, key and pointer handlers
    // that keep the state, and the ref.
    Props tela.Prop
    // Focused is true while the element has the keyboard focus (with
    // Within: or one of its descendants does), in an active window.
    Focused bool
    // FocusVisible is true while Focused and the focus came, or was last
    // moved, with the keyboard: Tela's focus-visible heuristic, Chromium's
    // (a text field matches it whatever moved the focus). A ring drawn
    // from FocusVisible does not flash when a button is clicked.
    FocusVisible bool
    // Ref is the ref attached to the element by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

FocusRingResult is what [`UseFocusRing`](#func-usefocusring) returns.

#### func UseFocusRing

```go
func UseFocusRing(o FocusRingOptions) FocusRingResult
```

UseFocusRing returns the props that track the focus of an element, and whether it should show a focus ring (React Aria's useFocusRing): the ring appears after the keyboard moves the focus and not after a click. The `focus:`, `focus-visible:` and `focus-within:` variants do the same for classes; use the hook when Go needs to know, or when a ring is made of several elements.

```go
ring := aria.UseFocusRing(aria.FocusRingOptions{})
return Button(ring.Props, Class("rounded-md px-3 py-1.5"),
    If(ring.FocusVisible, Class("ring-2 ring-primary")), Text("Save"))
```

The element must be focusable (a Button, an Input, or h.TabIndex).

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
field := func() tela.Node {
    ring := aria.UseFocusRing(aria.FocusRingOptions{})
    return Button(ring.Props, Class("px-3 py-1.5"),
        If(ring.FocusVisible, Text("Ring on")), If(!ring.FocusVisible, Text("Ring off")))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, field)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Ring off")) // a click does not show the ring
app.ExpectText("Ring off")
app.Press("Shift+Tab") // the keyboard does
app.Press("Tab")
app.ExpectText("Ring on")
fmt.Println("the ring follows the keyboard")
// Output: the ring follows the keyboard
```

### type FocusScopeOptions

```go
type FocusScopeOptions struct {
    // Contain keeps the focus inside the scope: Tab and Shift+Tab wrap
    // around its focusable elements instead of leaving, a press on
    // something that is not focusable (a scrim) leaves the focus where it
    // is, and a press or a script that would focus an element outside
    // keeps it inside instead (React Aria's contain). When the focused
    // element inside unmounts, the focus goes to the scope's element if it
    // is focusable (h.TabIndex(-1), as Radix's FocusScope focuses its
    // container), else to its first tabbable element. The content of
    // portals and overlays opened from inside the scope is inside it. The
    // most recently mounted containing scope wins.
    Contain bool
    // Restore gives the focus back when the scope unmounts, to the element
    // that had it when the scope mounted, if that element can still take
    // it.
    Restore bool
    // AutoFocus focuses the first tabbable element of the scope (the first
    // focusable one if none is tabbable) after the frame that mounts it,
    // unless the focus is already inside.
    AutoFocus bool
    // Ref is the element's ref, for a hook that is used together with
    // others on one element (see the package documentation); the zero
    // value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

FocusScopeOptions configures [`UseFocusScope`](#func-usefocusscope).

### type FocusScopeResult

```go
type FocusScopeResult struct {
    // Props go to the element that holds the scope: the scope itself and
    // the ref. The scope is the element's subtree (the content of the
    // portals rendered from inside it counts, after its own).
    Props tela.Prop
    // Manager moves the focus inside the scope.
    Manager FocusManager
    // Ref is the ref attached to the element by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

FocusScopeResult is what [`UseFocusScope`](#func-usefocusscope) returns.

#### func UseFocusScope

```go
func UseFocusScope(o FocusScopeOptions) FocusScopeResult
```

UseFocusScope returns the props that make an element a focus scope: contain Tab inside it (a dialog, a popover), restore the focus when it closes, focus its first element when it opens, and the manager that moves the focus inside it (React Aria's FocusScope and useFocusManager).

```go
scope := aria.UseFocusScope(aria.FocusScopeOptions{Contain: true, Restore: true, AutoFocus: true})
return Div(scope.Props, Role("dialog"), Class("rounded-lg p-4"), ...)
```

An arrow-key toolbar uses the manager from its key handler:

```go
scope := aria.UseFocusScope(aria.FocusScopeOptions{})
return Div(scope.Props, Role("toolbar"), OnKeyDown(func(e tela.KeyboardEvent) {
    switch e.Key {
    case tela.KeyArrowRight:
        e.PreventDefault()
        scope.Manager.FocusNext(aria.FocusOptions{Wrap: true})
    case tela.KeyArrowLeft:
        e.PreventDefault()
        scope.Manager.FocusPrevious(aria.FocusOptions{Wrap: true})
    }
}), ...)
```

The scope's element holds the hook's ref; see the package documentation when it must also hold other hooks'.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
page := func() tela.Node {
    open, setOpen := tela.UseState(false)
    return Div(
        Button(OnClick(func() { setOpen.Set(true) }), Text("Open")),
        If(open, tela.C(settingsDialog)))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Open"))
app.ExpectFocused(telatest.ByRole("button", "First")) // AutoFocus
app.Press("Tab")
app.Press("Tab")
app.ExpectFocused(telatest.ByRole("button", "First")) // Contain wraps around
fmt.Println("the focus stays inside the dialog")
// Output: the focus stays inside the dialog
```

### type HSB

```go
type HSB struct{ H, S, B, A float64 }
```

HSB is a color in the hue, saturation and brightness model (HSV, what a color picker's area shows). H is in degrees, from 0 to 360; S and B are percentages, from 0 to 100; A is the opacity, from 0 to 1.

The model keeps what RGB forgets: the hue of a gray (S is 0) and the hue and saturation of black (B is 0). That is why the color hooks keep an HSB in their [`ColorState`](#type-colorstate) and not the [`tela.Color`](API-Reference-tela#type-color) they report: a drag that passes through the gray axis does not lose the hue.

#### func ToHSB

```go
func ToHSB(c tela.Color) HSB
```

ToHSB returns c in the HSB model. The color is clamped to the sRGB gamut first. The hue of a gray is 0 (RGB does not have one): a caller that holds a hue keeps it itself, as [`ColorState`](#type-colorstate) does.

**Example**

```go
hsb := aria.ToHSB(tela.Hex("#336699"))
fmt.Printf("hue %.0f, saturation %.0f%%, brightness %.0f%%\n", hsb.H, hsb.S, hsb.B)
fmt.Println(aria.FormatHexColor(aria.HSB{H: 210, S: 66.667, B: 60, A: 1}.Color(), false))
// Output:
// hue 210, saturation 67%, brightness 60%
// #336699
```

#### func (HSB) Color

```go
func (c HSB) Color() tela.Color
```

Color returns c as a [`tela.Color`](API-Reference-tela#type-color) in the sRGB gamut. A hue of 360 is the hue of 0. Values out of range are clamped.

#### func (HSB) HSL

```go
func (c HSB) HSL() HSL
```

HSL returns the same color in the HSL model.

### type HSL

```go
type HSL struct{ H, S, L, A float64 }
```

HSL is a color in the hue, saturation and lightness model. H is in degrees, from 0 to 360; S and L are percentages, from 0 to 100; A is the opacity, from 0 to 1. Its saturation is not [`HSB`](#type-hsb)'s.

#### func ToHSL

```go
func ToHSL(c tela.Color) HSL
```

ToHSL returns c in the HSL model, with the clamping and the hue of [`ToHSB`](#func-tohsb).

#### func (HSL) Color

```go
func (c HSL) Color() tela.Color
```

Color returns c as a [`tela.Color`](API-Reference-tela#type-color) in the sRGB gamut. A hue of 360 is the hue of 0. Values out of range are clamped.

#### func (HSL) HSB

```go
func (c HSL) HSB() HSB
```

HSB returns the same color in the HSB model.

HoverEvent is passed to the callbacks of [`HoverOptions`](#type-hoveroptions).

```go
    // Disabled while hovered.
    OnHoverEnd func(HoverEvent)
```

### type HoverResult

```go
type HoverResult struct {
```
