#### func UseHover

```go
func UseHover(o HoverOptions) HoverResult
```

UseHover returns the props that track whether a mouse or a pen is over the element (React Aria's useHover). Unlike the `hover:` variant it reaches Go: show a tooltip, start a preview, drive an animation. It ignores touch: a finger does not hover, and the enter that a touch press makes is not a hover.

```go
hover := aria.UseHover(aria.HoverOptions{})
return Div(hover.Props, If(hover.Hovered, Class("ring-2")), Text("Card"))
```

Like the `hover:` variant, the element is hovered while the pointer is over it or its descendants.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
card := func() tela.Node {
    hover := aria.UseHover(aria.HoverOptions{})
    return Div(hover.Props, Class("h-20 w-40"),
        If(hover.Hovered, Text("Hovered")), If(!hover.Hovered, Text("Idle")))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, card)
app.ExpectText("Idle")
app.Hover(telatest.ByText("Idle"))
app.ExpectText("Hovered")
fmt.Println("hovered")
// Output: hovered
```

### type ListBoxOptions

```go
type ListBoxOptions[K comparable] struct {
    // Keys are the keys of the items, in the order they are shown. The
    // list must be given on every build; a key that goes takes its
    // selection with it only when the caller drops it (the focus moves to
    // the nearest item).
    Keys []K
    // TextValue is the text of an item, for typeahead (typing "ba" focuses
    // the first item whose text starts with it, ignoring case). Without
    // it the text of an item is its key as fmt.Sprint prints it, so
    // typeahead works for string keys; give TextValue when the keys are
    // IDs, or DisallowTypeAhead to turn typeahead off. While a search is
    // going (it expires after one second without keys) a Space is a
    // character of it and selects nothing, as in React Aria.
    TextValue func(K) string
    // DisabledKeys are the items that can not be focused, selected or
    // acted on. They are skipped by the keyboard, and get Disabled and
    // AriaDisabled, so both the `disabled:` and the `aria-disabled:`
    // variants match.
    DisabledKeys []K
    // SelectionMode is "none" (the default: the list has actions, not a
    // selection), "single" or "multiple".
    SelectionMode string
    // SelectionBehavior is "toggle" (the default: a click or Space toggles
    // the item, so several can be selected with plain clicks) or
    // "replace" (a click selects only that item, Ctrl+click toggles it,
    // Shift+click selects a range, and moving the focus with the arrow
    // keys moves the selection with it).
    SelectionBehavior string
    // Selected is the selection of a controlled list, with
    // OnSelectionChange asking for the next one. The zero Selection leaves
    // the selection to the hook, which starts at DefaultSelected. See
    // [Selection].
    Selected          Selection[K]
    DefaultSelected   Selection[K]
    OnSelectionChange func(Selection[K])
    // DisallowEmptySelection keeps one item selected once there is one.
    DisallowEmptySelection bool
    // DisallowSelectAll turns off Ctrl+A (Cmd+A on a Mac) in a multiple
    // selection.
    DisallowSelectAll bool
    // OnAction is called when an item is activated: with Enter, with a
    // tap, or with a click when nothing is selected (SelectionBehavior
    // "toggle") or the list does not select (SelectionMode "none"). With
    // SelectionBehavior "replace" and a selection, a click selects and a
    // double click or Enter runs the action.
    OnAction func(K)
    // Orientation is "vertical" (the default; ArrowUp and ArrowDown move
    // the focus) or "horizontal" (ArrowLeft and ArrowRight).
    Orientation string
    // Direction is "ltr" (the default) or "rtl": the arrow keys of a
    // horizontal list swap in a right-to-left one.
    Direction string
    // ShouldFocusWrap makes ArrowDown on the last item focus the first,
    // and ArrowUp on the first the last.
    ShouldFocusWrap bool
    // ShouldUseVirtualFocus keeps the focus on the list itself and
    // marks the focused item with aria-activedescendant, as a combobox's
    // popup does: items are not focusable, and IsFocused(k) says which one
    // is highlighted.
    ShouldUseVirtualFocus bool
    // ExternalFocus is ShouldUseVirtualFocus for a list that never has
    // the focus: another element does (a combobox's input), and calls
    // [Collection.HandleKeyDown] from its key handler and puts
    // [Collection.ActiveDescendant] on itself. The list is not a tab stop
    // and pressing an item does not move the focus away from that element.
    // The keys of a text field stay its own: HandleKeyDown handles the
    // arrow keys, PageUp, PageDown and Enter, and there is no typeahead.
    ExternalFocus bool
    // ShouldFocusOnHover focuses an item when the mouse moves over it.
    ShouldFocusOnHover bool
    // DisallowTypeAhead turns off typeahead.
    DisallowTypeAhead bool
    // EscapeKeyBehavior is "clearSelection" (the default: Escape clears
    // the selection, and is not passed on while there is one) or "none".
    EscapeKeyBehavior string
    // AutoFocus focuses the list when it mounts: the first selected item
    // if there is one, else the item FocusStrategy says, else the list.
    AutoFocus bool
    // FocusStrategy is FocusFirst or FocusLast: it implies AutoFocus.
    FocusStrategy string
    // AriaLabel and AriaLabelledBy name the list.
    AriaLabel      string
    AriaLabelledBy tela.ElementRef
    // Ref is the list's ref, for a hook that is used together with others
    // on one element (see the package documentation) and for a
    // VirtualList: the list scrolls its items into view through it. The
    // zero value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

ListBoxOptions configures [`UseListBox`](#func-uselistbox). K is the type of the items' keys: a string, an int, an ID type; any comparable value.

### type ListBoxResult

```go
type ListBoxResult[K comparable] struct {
    Collection[K]
    // Props go to the list's element: the "listbox" role, aria-multiselectable,
    // the ref, the key handler and, with a roving focus, a tab stop while
    // no item is focused. Give them to the element that scrolls (or to a
    // h.VirtualList).
    Props tela.Prop
    // Selected is the current selection (for a single selection, its
    // [Selection.First] is the selected key).
    Selected Selection[K]
    // Ref is the ref attached to the list by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

ListBoxResult is what [`UseListBox`](#func-uselistbox) returns.

#### func UseListBox

```go
func UseListBox[K comparable](o ListBoxOptions[K]) ListBoxResult[K]
```

UseListBox holds the state of a list box and returns the props of its element and its options (React Aria's useListBox with useListState, useSelectableList and useOption): a keyed collection with a focused key, a selection, and the keyboard and pointer rules of a listbox.

```go
var fruit = []string{"apple", "banana", "cherry"}

lb := aria.UseListBox(aria.ListBoxOptions[string]{
    Keys: fruit, TextValue: strings.ToUpper, SelectionMode: "single",
    AriaLabel: "Fruit",
})
return Div(lb.Props, Class("w-48 rounded-md border p-1"),
    h.Range(len(fruit), func(i int) tela.Node {
        k := fruit[i]
        return Div(lb.ItemProps(k), Key(k),
            Class("rounded px-2 py-1 aria-selected:bg-primary aria-selected:text-primary-foreground focus-visible:ring-2"),
            Text(k))
    }))
```

The keyboard: ArrowUp and ArrowDown (ArrowLeft and ArrowRight for a horizontal list) move the focus, skipping disabled items, with ShouldFocusWrap going around the ends; Home and End jump; PageUp and PageDown move a viewport of items; typing text focuses the next item that starts with it (the string expires after a second); Space and Enter select or act; with a multiple selection Shift+ArrowDown extends the range, Ctrl+A selects everything and Ctrl+ArrowDown moves without selecting (with SelectionBehavior "replace"). A click selects, Shift+click extends, Ctrl+click toggles.

Style items with the `aria-selected:` and `aria-disabled:` variants, with `focus-visible:` (the element that has the focus), or in Go from IsSelected, IsFocused and IsDisabled. The list uses a roving focus: the focused item's element has the focus of the window and is the list's only tab stop. Render the items as Divs or Lis, not Buttons.

##### Selection

The selection is a [`Selection`](#type-selection). A list keeps it itself by default:

```go
aria.ListBoxOptions[string]{Keys: fruit, SelectionMode: "multiple",
    DefaultSelected: aria.SelectionOf("banana")}
```

and is controlled by passing the selection, next to the callback that asks for changes (OnSelectionChange is also called for an uncontrolled list):

```go
sel, setSel := tela.UseState(aria.SelectionOf("banana"))
aria.ListBoxOptions[string]{Keys: fruit, SelectionMode: "multiple",
    Selected: sel, OnSelectionChange: setSel.Set}
```

Ctrl+A passes [`All`](#func-all); resolve it with [`Selection.Resolve`](#func-selectionk-resolve) to get keys.

##### Long lists

A h.VirtualList works as the list: give it Props and render its items with ItemProps. Keys that are not rendered can be focused: the list scrolls to their index and the item takes the focus when it mounts. PageUp and PageDown measure the rendered items. Typeahead and Ctrl+A work on the whole list.

```go
h.VirtualList(len(keys), func(int) float32 { return 32 }, func(i int) tela.Node {
    return Div(lb.ItemProps(keys[i]), Key(keys[i]), Class("h-8"), Text(keys[i]))
}, lb.Props, Class("h-64"))
```

##### Sections

Section returns the props of a group of items and of its heading, which names the group: the keys stay one flat list.

**Example**

```go
names := []string{"apple", "banana", "cherry"}
page := func() tela.Node {
    lb := aria.UseListBox(aria.ListBoxOptions[string]{
        Keys: names, TextValue: strings.ToUpper, SelectionMode: "single", AriaLabel: "Fruit",
    })
    return Div(lb.Props, Class("w-48 rounded-md border p-1"),
        Range(len(names), func(i int) tela.Node {
            k := names[i]
            return Div(lb.ItemProps(k), Key(k),
                Class("rounded px-2 py-1 aria-selected:bg-primary aria-selected:text-primary-foreground focus-visible:ring-2"),
                Text(k))
        }))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(300, 200))
app.Press("Tab")
app.Press("ArrowDown")
app.Press("Enter")
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - listbox "Fruit":
//   - option "apple"
//   - option "banana" [selected]
//   - option "cherry"
```

**Example (controlled)**

```go
// A multiple selection that the app keeps, with the other half of the
// page reading it.
names := []string{"apple", "banana", "cherry"}
page := func() tela.Node {
    sel, setSel := tela.UseState(aria.SelectionOf("banana"))
    lb := aria.UseListBox(aria.ListBoxOptions[string]{
        Keys: names, SelectionMode: "multiple", AriaLabel: "Fruit",
        Selected: sel, OnSelectionChange: setSel.Set,
    })
    return Div(
        Div(lb.Props, Range(len(names), func(i int) tela.Node {
            return Div(lb.ItemProps(names[i]), Key(names[i]), Class("h-8"), Text(names[i]))
        })),
        Textf("%d selected", sel.Resolve(names).Len()))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(300, 200))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("option", "cherry"))
app.Press("Control+a")
app.ExpectText("3 selected")
fmt.Println("3 selected")
// Output: 3 selected
```

### type MenuBarOptions

```go
type MenuBarOptions[K comparable] struct {
    // Keys are the keys of the menus, in the order their triggers are
    // shown. The list must be given on every build.
    Keys []K
    // DisabledKeys are the triggers that can not be focused or opened.
    DisabledKeys []K
    // Disabled disables every trigger.
    Disabled bool
    // Open points to the open menu of a controlled bar; nil leaves it to
    // the hook, which starts with DefaultOpen (nil: all closed).
    Open        *K
    DefaultOpen *K
    // OnOpenChange is called with the menu that opened (open true) or the
    // menu that closed (open false). Moving from one menu to another calls
    // it once, with the one that opens. It is also called for an
    // uncontrolled bar.
    OnOpenChange func(key K, open bool)
    // Direction is "ltr" (the default) or "rtl", which swaps ArrowLeft and
    // ArrowRight.
    Direction string
    // NoWrap keeps ArrowLeft and ArrowRight from going around the ends of
    // the bar (the pattern wraps).
    NoWrap bool
    // AriaLabel names the bar; else it is named by AriaLabelledBy.
    AriaLabel      string
    AriaLabelledBy tela.ElementRef
    // Ref is the bar element's ref, for a hook used together with others on
    // the same element; the zero value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

MenuBarOptions configures [`UseMenuBar`](#func-usemenubar): a row of menu triggers, such as the File, Edit and View of an application. K is the type of the menus' keys; the triggers are keyed like the items of a list box (see [`ListBoxOptions`](#type-listboxoptions) for Keys and DisabledKeys).

The open menu is a key, uncontrolled when Open is nil (the hook keeps it, starting at DefaultOpen) and controlled when Open points to it: the bar shows it and only asks OnOpenChange for the next one. A key that is not in Keys (the zero value of K, say) means that no menu is open.

### type MenuBarResult

```go
type MenuBarResult[K comparable] struct {
    // Props go to the bar's element: the "menubar" role, its orientation,
    // its name and the ref.
    Props tela.Prop
    // Open is whether a menu is open, and OpenKey which one (the zero value
    // of K when none is).
    Open    bool
    OpenKey K
    // FocusStrategy is where the focus goes when the open menu mounts:
    // [FocusFirst], [FocusLast], or "" for the menu itself (opened with a
    // pointer). Pass it to [MenuOptions].FocusStrategy.
    FocusStrategy string
    // Close closes the open menu, if any: pass it to [MenuOptions].OnClose
    // so that choosing an item closes the menu.
    Close func()
    // Ref is the ref attached to the bar by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

MenuBarResult is what [`UseMenuBar`](#func-usemenubar) returns.

#### func UseMenuBar

```go
func UseMenuBar[K comparable](o MenuBarOptions[K]) MenuBarResult[K]
```

UseMenuBar holds the state of a menu bar and returns the props of the bar and of its triggers and menus (the WAI-ARIA menubar pattern with React Aria's menu trigger behavior), on top of [`UseMenu`](#func-usemenu) and [`UsePopover`](#func-usepopover). Only one menu is open at a time, so the hook is called once, and the menu that is open is rendered by a component of its own, in a Portal:

```go
bar := aria.UseMenuBar(aria.MenuBarOptions[string]{Keys: []string{"file", "edit"}, AriaLabel: "Application"})
return Fragment(
    Div(bar.Props, Class("flex gap-1"),
        h.Range(len(titles), func(i int) tela.Node {
            k := keys[i]
            return Button(bar.TriggerProps(k), Key(k), Class("rounded px-3 py-1 aria-expanded:bg-accent"), Text(titles[k]))
        })),
    Portal(If(bar.Open, tela.WithKey(appMenu{bar}, bar.OpenKey))))

type appMenu struct{ bar aria.MenuBarResult[string] }

func (m appMenu) Build() tela.Node {
    k := m.bar.OpenKey
    pop := aria.UsePopover(m.bar.PopoverOptions(k))
    menu := aria.UseMenu(aria.MenuOptions[string]{
        Keys: items[k], OnAction: run, OnClose: m.bar.Close,
        AutoFocus: true, FocusStrategy: m.bar.FocusStrategy, Ref: m.bar.MenuRef(k),
    })
    return Div(pop.Props, m.bar.MenuProps(k), menu.Props, Class("w-48 rounded-md border bg-popover p-1"), ...)
}
```

The component has the open key as its key, so that each menu mounts anew and focuses its first item. The triggers are "menuitem"s with aria-haspopup and aria-expanded, and the bar is one tab stop that remembers its last trigger. ArrowLeft and ArrowRight (swapped by Direction "rtl") move the focus between the triggers, wrapping unless NoWrap, and Home and End jump; ArrowDown, Enter and Space open the menu of the focused trigger on its first item, ArrowUp on its last. While a menu is open ArrowLeft and ArrowRight close it and open the neighbor's, and hovering another trigger opens its menu: that is why the popover is not modal. A press on the open menu's trigger closes it, so do Escape, a press outside, and Tab, which also leaves the bar. Closing gives the focus back to the trigger.

There are no submenus, no typeahead on the triggers and no mnemonics.

**Example**

```go
// A menu bar: ArrowDown opens the File menu on its first item, ArrowRight
// moves to the Edit menu.
var ev events
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, barPage(aria.MenuBarOptions[string]{}, &ev), telatest.Size(400, 300))
app.Focus(trigger("File"))
app.Press("ArrowDown")
app.Press("ArrowRight")
app.ExpectFocused(menuitem("Undo"))
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - button "Before"
// - menubar "Application":
//   - menuitem "File"
//   - menuitem "Edit" [expanded]
//   - menuitem "View"
// - button "After"
// - menu "Edit":
//   - menuitem "Undo"
//   - menuitem "Redo"
```

#### func (MenuBarResult[K]) IsOpen

```go
func (r MenuBarResult[K]) IsOpen(k K) bool
```

IsOpen reports whether the menu with key k is open.

#### func (MenuBarResult[K]) MenuProps

```go
func (r MenuBarResult[K]) MenuProps(k K) tela.Prop
```

MenuProps returns the props of the element of the menu with key k: its ref, aria-labelledby (the trigger), a focus scope that gives the focus back to the trigger when the menu closes, and the keys that move between the menus: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight open the neighbor's menu and Tab closes the menu and leaves the bar. Give them next to the popover's props and [`UseMenu`](#func-usemenu)'s.

#### func (MenuBarResult[K]) MenuRef

```go
func (r MenuBarResult[K]) MenuRef(k K) tela.ElementRef
```

MenuRef returns the ref of the menu with key k: pass it as [`MenuOptions`](#type-menuoptions).Ref; [`MenuBarResult.MenuProps`](#func-menubarresultk-menuprops) and PopoverOptions share it.

#### func (MenuBarResult[K]) PopoverOptions

```go
func (r MenuBarResult[K]) PopoverOptions(k K) PopoverOptions
```

PopoverOptions returns the options of [`UsePopover`](#func-usepopover) for the menu with key k: anchored below its trigger ("bottom-start"), open, closed through the bar, and not modal, so that the other triggers stay under the pointer: a press on any trigger is the trigger's own and not a press outside. Change what you need in the value returned (Offset, Floating).

#### func (MenuBarResult[K]) SetOpen

```go
func (r MenuBarResult[K]) SetOpen(k K, open bool)
```

SetOpen opens the menu with key k (focusing the menu itself, as a pointer does), or closes it. It does nothing for a disabled or unknown key.

#### func (MenuBarResult[K]) TriggerProps

```go
func (r MenuBarResult[K]) TriggerProps(k K) tela.Prop
```

TriggerProps returns the props of the trigger with key k: the "menuitem" role, aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and, while its menu is open, aria-controls; the ref, the disabled state, a tab stop on the trigger that had the focus last (else the first enabled one) and the handlers: a press opens the menu (a mouse or a pen on the press, a touch on the release) or closes it, hovering opens it while another menu is open, and the keys listed in [`UseMenuBar`](#func-usemenubar) work.

Render the trigger with a Button, or with any element that should behave as one.

#### func (MenuBarResult[K]) TriggerRef

```go
func (r MenuBarResult[K]) TriggerRef(k K) tela.ElementRef
```

TriggerRef returns the ref that TriggerProps(k) attaches to the trigger with key k, to share with another hook on its element.

### type MenuOptions

```go
type MenuOptions[K comparable] struct {
    Keys []K
    // TextValue is the text of an item, for typeahead; the key as
    // fmt.Sprint prints it when nil. See [ListBoxOptions].
    TextValue    func(K) string
    DisabledKeys []K
    // SelectionMode is "none" (the default: the items are commands,
    // "menuitem"), "single" (radio items, "menuitemradio", of which one
    // is selected) or "multiple" (checkbox items, "menuitemcheckbox").
    // A single selection keeps one item selected once there is one.
    SelectionMode     string
    Selected          Selection[K]
    DefaultSelected   Selection[K]
    OnSelectionChange func(Selection[K])
    // OnAction is called with the key of an item when it is chosen (a
    // click, Enter or Space), whether the menu selects or not.
    OnAction func(K)
    // OnClose is called when choosing an item should close the menu: pass
    // the trigger's Close. See CloseOnSelect.
    OnClose func()
    // CloseOnSelect decides whether choosing an item calls OnClose: nil
    // (the default) closes the menu unless the selection is "multiple",
    // where several items are toggled in a row; point to true or false to
    // decide.
    CloseOnSelect *bool
    // AutoFocus focuses the menu when it mounts, and FocusStrategy
    // (FocusFirst, FocusLast, from the trigger's result) the item that
    // takes the focus; a selected item wins. A menu that mounts when it
    // opens passes AutoFocus: true and the trigger's FocusStrategy; a
    // non-empty FocusStrategy alone implies AutoFocus.
    AutoFocus     bool
    FocusStrategy string
    // ShouldFocusWrap makes the arrow keys go around the ends.
    ShouldFocusWrap bool
    Direction       string
    // DisallowTypeAhead turns off typeahead.
    DisallowTypeAhead bool
    // AriaLabel names the menu; the trigger's MenuProps already name it
    // by the trigger.
    AriaLabel string
    // Ref is the menu's ref: pass the trigger's MenuRef, which its
    // MenuProps attach too.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

MenuOptions configures [`UseMenu`](#func-usemenu). The items are keyed like those of a list box: see [`ListBoxOptions`](#type-listboxoptions) for Keys, TextValue, DisabledKeys, Selected, DefaultSelected, OnSelectionChange, ShouldFocusWrap and Direction.

### type MenuResult

```go
type MenuResult[K comparable] struct {
    Collection[K]
    // Props go to the menu's element: the "menu" role, the ref, the key
    // handler and a tab stop for the menu itself while no item is
    // focused. Give them next to the trigger's MenuProps and the popover's
    // props.
    Props tela.Prop
    // Selected is the current selection.
    Selected Selection[K]
    // Ref is the ref attached to the menu by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

MenuResult is what [`UseMenu`](#func-usemenu) returns.

#### func UseMenu

```go
func UseMenu[K comparable](o MenuOptions[K]) MenuResult[K]
```

UseMenu holds the state of a menu and returns the props of its element and its items (React Aria's useMenu, useMenuItem and useMenuSection with useTreeState). It is the collection of a menu button: it takes the trigger's results, focuses the first or last item as the trigger says, chooses with Enter, Space and clicks, closes the menu, and the focus returns to the trigger by the scope of the trigger's MenuProps (UseMenu adds none).

Call it in the component that is rendered while the menu is open: it focuses an item when it mounts, so a menu that stays mounted while closed would not focus again.

```go
mt := aria.UseMenuTrigger(aria.MenuTriggerOptions{})
pop := aria.UsePopover(aria.PopoverOptions{
    Trigger: mt.Ref, Ref: mt.MenuRef, Open: mt.Open, OnClose: mt.Close,
    Placement: "bottom-start", Modal: true,
})
return Fragment(
    Button(mt.TriggerProps, Text("Actions")),
    Portal(If(mt.Open, actionMenu{mt, pop})))

type actionMenu struct{ mt aria.MenuTriggerResult; pop aria.PopoverResult }

func (m actionMenu) Build() tela.Node {
    menu := aria.UseMenu(aria.MenuOptions[string]{
        Keys: actions, TextValue: strings.ToUpper,
        OnAction: run, OnClose: m.mt.Close,
        AutoFocus: true, FocusStrategy: m.mt.FocusStrategy, Ref: m.mt.MenuRef,
    })
    return Div(m.pop.Props, m.mt.MenuProps, menu.Props, Class("w-48 rounded-md border bg-popover p-1"),
        h.Range(len(actions), func(i int) tela.Node {
            return Div(menu.ItemProps(actions[i]), Key(actions[i]),
                Class("rounded px-2 py-1.5 focus-visible:bg-accent aria-disabled:opacity-50"), Text(actions[i]))
        }))
}
```

Items with SelectionMode "single" or "multiple" are radio and checkbox items: they print as `menuitemradio "Name" [checked]` and `menuitemcheckbox "Name" [checked]`, and `aria-checked:` styles them. The mouse focuses the item under it, as in a native menu. Disabled items are skipped. Submenus are not part of this hook.

**Example**

```go
// A menu button: ArrowDown opens the menu with the first item focused,
// Enter chooses it, the menu closes and the focus goes back.
var ev events
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, menuApp(aria.MenuOptions[string]{}, &ev), telatest.Size(400, 300))
trigger := telatest.ByRole("button", "Actions")
app.Focus(trigger)
app.Press("ArrowDown")
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Press("Enter")
app.ExpectFocused(trigger)
fmt.Println(ev.take())
// Output:
// - menu "Actions":
//   - menuitem "Edit"
//   - menuitem "Duplicate"
//   - menuitem "Archive"
//   - menuitem "Delete"
// action:edit
```

### type MenuTriggerOptions

```go
type MenuTriggerOptions struct {
    // Trigger is how a pointer opens the menu: "press" (the default), at
    // the press of a mouse or a pen and at the release of a touch, or
    // "longPress", when the press lasts, which leaves the quick press of the
    // trigger to OnPress; the keyboard then opens it with Alt+ArrowDown and
    // Alt+ArrowUp only. Another value panics in dev mode.
    Trigger string
    // Type is what the trigger opens: "menu" (the default) or "listbox".
    Type string
    // Open points to the open state of a controlled menu; nil leaves the
    // state to the hook, starting at DefaultOpen. OnOpenChange is called
    // with the next state: for a controlled menu it is how the change is
    // asked for, for an uncontrolled one a notification.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)
    // Disabled makes the trigger inert and disabled.
    Disabled bool
    // OnPress is the trigger's own press with Trigger "longPress"; it does
    // not run after a long press that opened the menu.
    OnPress func(PressEvent)
    // Ref is the trigger's ref and MenuRef the menu's, for hooks used
    // together with others on the same element; the zero value makes the
    // hook create its own.
    Ref, MenuRef tela.ElementRef
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

MenuTriggerOptions configures [`UseMenuTrigger`](#func-usemenutrigger).

### type MenuTriggerResult

```go
type MenuTriggerResult struct {
    // TriggerProps go to the trigger: the press (and long press), the
    // keyboard that opens the menu, the "button" role, a tab stop,
    // aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and, while open, aria-controls.
    TriggerProps tela.Prop
    // MenuProps go to the menu's element: the ref, aria-labelledby (the
    // trigger) and a focus scope that gives the focus back to the trigger
    // when the menu closes. The menu's other hooks and [UsePopover] share
    // MenuRef.
    MenuProps tela.Prop
    // Open is whether the menu is open.
    Open bool
    // FocusStrategy is where the focus goes when the menu opens: [FocusFirst],
    // [FocusLast], or "" for the menu itself (opened with a mouse or a
    // touch). The menu focuses accordingly when it mounts.
    FocusStrategy string
    // SetOpen asks for a state, Toggle for the other one and Close for
    // closed. A menu closes itself when an item is chosen by calling Close.
    SetOpen func(open bool)
    Toggle  func()
    Close   func()
    // Pressed is true while the trigger is pressed.
    Pressed bool
    // Ref is the trigger's ref and MenuRef the menu's.
    Ref, MenuRef tela.ElementRef
}
```

MenuTriggerResult is what [`UseMenuTrigger`](#func-usemenutrigger) returns.

#### func UseMenuTrigger

```go
func UseMenuTrigger(o MenuTriggerOptions) MenuTriggerResult
```

UseMenuTrigger holds the open state of a menu and returns the props of its trigger (React Aria's useMenuTrigger with useMenuTriggerState): a press opens it, and so do Enter, Space and ArrowDown (focusing the first item) and ArrowUp (the last), or a long press with Trigger "longPress".

```go
mt := aria.UseMenuTrigger(aria.MenuTriggerOptions{})
pop := aria.UsePopover(aria.PopoverOptions{
    Trigger: mt.Ref, Ref: mt.MenuRef, Open: mt.Open, OnClose: mt.Close,
    Placement: "bottom-start", Modal: true,
})
return Fragment(
    Button(mt.TriggerProps, Text("Actions")),
    Portal(If(mt.Open, Div(pop.Props, mt.MenuProps, Role("menu"), ...))))
```

The menu itself, its items and keyboard navigation belong to the menu collection hook (UseMenu); this hook gives it the focus strategy and Close, to call when an item is chosen.

**Example**

```go
// ArrowDown opens the menu focusing its first item, ArrowUp its last.
page := func() tela.Node {
    mt := aria.UseMenuTrigger(aria.MenuTriggerOptions{})
    pop := aria.UsePopover(aria.PopoverOptions{
        Trigger: mt.Ref, Ref: mt.MenuRef, Open: mt.Open, OnClose: mt.Close, Placement: "bottom-start", Modal: true,
    })
    return Div(Class("relative h-full"),
        Button(mt.TriggerProps, Class("absolute left-4 top-4 h-8 w-24"), Text("Actions")),
        Portal(If(mt.Open,
            Div(pop.Props, mt.MenuProps, Role("menu"), Class("w-40 bg-white"),
                Textf("focus the %s item", mt.FocusStrategy)))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(400, 300))
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("button", "Actions"))
app.Press("ArrowDown")
app.ExpectText("focus the first item")
app.Press("Escape")
app.Press("ArrowUp")
app.ExpectText("focus the last item")
fmt.Println("ArrowDown: first, ArrowUp: last")
// Output: ArrowDown: first, ArrowUp: last
```

### type MeterOptions

```go
type MeterOptions struct {
    // Value is the measure, from Min to Max.
    Value float64
    // Min and Max are the ends of the scale. Min is 0 by default and Max
    // 100 when both are 0.
    Min, Max float64
    // FormatValue returns Value as people read it, for aria-valuetext; the
    // default is the percentage, rounded ("40%").
    FormatValue func(float64) string
    // AriaLabel names the meter; else it is named by the element with
    // LabelProps, or by AriaLabelledBy.
    AriaLabel string
    // AriaLabelledBy is the element that names the meter, when it is not
    // the one with LabelProps.
    AriaLabelledBy tela.ElementRef
}
```

MeterOptions configures [`UseMeter`](#func-usemeter): a measure within a known range, such as disk usage, as opposed to the progress of a task. The fields are those of [`ProgressBarOptions`](#type-progressbaroptions) without Indeterminate.

### type OffsetOptions

```go
type OffsetOptions struct {
    // CrossAxis moves the element along the anchor's edge, so that it
    // skids away from the alignment (Floating UI's crossAxis). Positive
    // moves it right for the top and bottom sides, down for the left and
    // right ones (mirrored in a right-to-left element for the top and
    // bottom sides).
    CrossAxis float32
    // AlignmentAxis replaces CrossAxis for aligned placements ("-start",
    // "-end") when HasAlignmentAxis is set: positive moves the element
    // toward the inside of the anchor's edge from the start and, negated,
    // from the end (Floating UI's alignmentAxis, which is a number or null).
    AlignmentAxis    float32
    HasAlignmentAxis bool
}
```

OffsetOptions are the options of [`Offset`](#func-offset) beyond the distance.

### type OverlayOptions

```go
type OverlayOptions struct {
    // Open is whether the overlay is open. A closed overlay is not on the
    // overlay stack: its Props do nothing. Render the overlay only while
    // it is open, and pass the same value here, or true when the
    // component that calls the hook exists only while the overlay does.
    Open bool
    // OnClose is called when the user asks to close the overlay: Escape,
    // a press outside it (with Dismissable) or the focus leaving it (with
    // ShouldCloseOnBlur). The caller closes it, by changing the state that
    // Open comes from.
    OnClose func()
    // Dismissable closes the overlay with a press outside it: at the
    // pointer down, the press is kept from the elements under it, and at
    // the release OnClose is called and the click the press would make is
    // cancelled (React Aria's isDismissable). An alert dialog is not
    // dismissable.
    Dismissable bool
    // KeyboardDismissDisabled keeps Escape from closing the overlay. The
    // overlay still takes the key while it is the top one: Escape does not
    // reach the overlays below it nor the page.
    KeyboardDismissDisabled bool
    // ShouldCloseOnBlur closes the overlay when the focus moves from
    // inside it to another element outside it (not when it goes nowhere,
    // such as the window losing the focus).
    ShouldCloseOnBlur bool
    // ShouldCloseOnInteractOutside decides, for a press outside the
    // overlay, whether it closes it; nil closes it for every press. The
    // event carries the position of the press in the window: a popover
    // excludes its trigger by comparing it with the trigger's bounds. It
    // applies to Dismissable overlays.
    ShouldCloseOnInteractOutside func(tela.PointerEvent) bool
    // Modal makes everything outside the overlay inert while it is open
    // and the topmost modal overlay (the overlays opened from it stay
    // usable): it cannot be pressed or focused, is out of the Tab order and
    // is hidden from the aria snapshot (React Aria's ariaHideOutside).
    // A dialog is modal; a popover, a menu or a toast usually is not.
    Modal bool
}
```

OverlayOptions configures [`UseOverlay`](#func-useoverlay).

### type OverlayResult

```go
type OverlayResult struct {
    // Props go to the overlay's element: they put it on the overlay stack
    // while it is mounted and Open, so that Escape and presses outside
    // reach only the top overlay, and make it modal if asked.
    Props tela.Prop
}
```

OverlayResult is what [`UseOverlay`](#func-useoverlay) returns.

#### func UseOverlay

```go
func UseOverlay(o OverlayOptions) OverlayResult
```

UseOverlay returns the props that make an element an overlay (React Aria's useOverlay and, with Modal, useModalOverlay): the topmost one is closed by Escape and by a press outside it, and a modal one makes the rest of the window inert. Overlays opened from inside another count as inside it (a popover in a dialog, in a Portal or not), so pressing in the popover does not close the dialog, and Escape closes the popover first.

```go
func Confirm(open bool, close func()) tela.Node {
    ov := aria.UseOverlay(aria.OverlayOptions{Open: open, OnClose: close, Dismissable: true, Modal: true})
    return Portal(Presence(If(open,
        Div(ov.Props, Exit("opacity-0"), Class("... transition starting:opacity-0"), ...))))
}
```

Use [`UseDialog`](#func-usedialog) on the same element for the dialog role and the focus, and [`UseOverlayTrigger`](#func-useoverlaytrigger) for the state and the trigger. Rendering it inside a Presence lets it fade out: an exiting overlay is inert and no longer on the stack, so the page below is usable at once and a second Escape reaches the next overlay.

The hook has no ref: [`FocusScopeOptions.Ref`](#type-focusscopeoptions) and the other hooks that share the element take theirs as usual.

**Example**

```go
// A modal overlay: Escape and a press outside close it, and the page
// below is inert while it is open.
page := func() tela.Node {
    open, setOpen := tela.UseState(true)
    ov := aria.UseOverlay(aria.OverlayOptions{
        Open: open, OnClose: func() { setOpen.Set(false) }, Dismissable: true, Modal: true,
    })
    return Div(Class("relative h-full"),
        Button(Class("h-8 w-24"), Text("Page")),
        If(open, Div(ov.Props, Class("absolute left-[100px] top-[100px] h-20 w-40 bg-white"), Text("Overlay"))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(300, 200))
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
app.Press("Escape")
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - text: Overlay
// - button "Page"
```

### type OverlayTriggerOptions

```go
type OverlayTriggerOptions struct {
    // Type is what the trigger opens: "dialog" (the default), "menu",
    // "listbox", "tree" or "grid" (the values of aria-haspopup). Another
    // value panics in dev mode with the closest valid one.
    Type string
    // Open points to the open state of a controlled overlay; nil leaves the
    // state to the hook, starting at DefaultOpen. OnOpenChange is called
    // with the next state when the trigger or the overlay asks for a change:
    // for a controlled overlay it is how the change is asked for, for an
    // uncontrolled one a notification.
    Open         *bool
    DefaultOpen  bool
    OnOpenChange func(open bool)
    // Disabled makes the trigger inert and disabled.
    Disabled bool
    // Ref is the trigger's ref, for a hook used together with others on the
    // same element; the zero value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
    // OverlayRef is the overlay's ref, which the trigger's aria-controls
    // points to; the zero value makes the hook create its own. The hooks of
    // the overlay's element (UsePopover, UseDialog, UseFocusScope...) must
    // share it as their Ref option.
    OverlayRef tela.ElementRef
}
```

OverlayTriggerOptions configures [`UseOverlayTrigger`](#func-useoverlaytrigger).

### type OverlayTriggerResult

```go
type OverlayTriggerResult struct {
    // TriggerProps go to the trigger: a press that toggles the overlay,
    // the "button" role, a tab stop, aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and,
    // while the overlay is open, aria-controls. Override the role on an
    // element that is not a button.
    TriggerProps tela.Prop
    // OverlayProps go to the overlay's element when no other hook of the
    // element attaches the overlay's ref: they hold just that ref.
    OverlayProps tela.Prop
    // Open is the current state, controlled or not.
    Open bool
    // SetOpen asks for a state (a controlled overlay only reports it to
    // OnOpenChange), Toggle for the other one, and Close for closed; Open
    // for open is SetOpen(true).
    SetOpen func(open bool)
    Toggle  func()
    Close   func()
    // Pressed is true while the trigger is pressed.
    Pressed bool
    // Ref is the trigger's ref and OverlayRef the overlay's.
    Ref, OverlayRef tela.ElementRef
}
```

OverlayTriggerResult is what [`UseOverlayTrigger`](#func-useoverlaytrigger) returns.

#### func UseOverlayTrigger

```go
func UseOverlayTrigger(o OverlayTriggerOptions) OverlayTriggerResult
```

UseOverlayTrigger holds the open state of an overlay and returns the props of its trigger (React Aria's useOverlayTrigger with useOverlayTriggerState): a press toggles the overlay, and the trigger says what it opens (aria-haspopup), whether it is open (aria-expanded) and which element it controls (aria-controls).

```go
trig := aria.UseOverlayTrigger(aria.OverlayTriggerOptions{Type: "dialog"})
ov := aria.UseOverlay(aria.OverlayOptions{Open: trig.Open, OnClose: trig.Close, Dismissable: true})
return Fragment(
    Button(trig.TriggerProps, Class("rounded-md border px-3 py-1.5"), Text("Share")),
    Portal(If(trig.Open,
        Div(ov.Props, trig.OverlayProps, Role("dialog"), Text("Link copied")))))
```

The state is uncontrolled by default; pass Open for a controlled one. Pair it with [`UsePopover`](#func-usepopover) or [`UseOverlay`](#func-useoverlay) and [`UseDialog`](#func-usedialog) for the overlay (sharing OverlayRef), and with [`UseMenuTrigger`](#func-usemenutrigger) for a menu.

**Example**

```go
// The trigger holds the state and says what it opens and whether it is
// open; OnOpenChange follows an uncontrolled overlay.
page := func() tela.Node {
    log, setLog := tela.UseState("")
    trig := aria.UseOverlayTrigger(aria.OverlayTriggerOptions{
        Type:         "menu",
        OnOpenChange: func(open bool) { setLog.Set(fmt.Sprintf("open=%v", open)) },
    })
    return Div(
        Button(trig.TriggerProps, Text("Actions")),
        If(trig.Open, Div(Ref(trig.OverlayRef), Text("Items"))),
        Text(log))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(300, 200))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Actions"))
app.Expect(telatest.ByRole("button", "Actions"), telatest.Expanded(true))
app.ExpectText("open=true")
fmt.Println("open=true")
// Output: open=true
```

### type PointerType

```go
type PointerType string
```

PointerType is the device or the way a press, or a hover, came from.

```go
const (
    // PointerMouse is a mouse or a touchpad.
    PointerMouse PointerType = "mouse"
    // PointerTouch is a finger on a touchscreen.
    PointerTouch PointerType = "touch"
    // PointerPen is a stylus.
    PointerPen PointerType = "pen"
    // PointerKeyboard is a press made with Enter or Space on the focused
    // element.
    PointerKeyboard PointerType = "keyboard"
    // PointerVirtual is a click that no pointer or key made: an assistive
    // technology or an agent (the "click" action of the semantics tree),
    // or the click a Label sends to the control it labels.
    PointerVirtual PointerType = "virtual"
)
```

The pointer types.

### type PopoverOptions

```go
type PopoverOptions struct {
    // Trigger is the ref of the element the popover is anchored to, the
    // trigger that opens it ([OverlayTriggerResult].Ref).
    Trigger tela.ElementRef
    // Open is whether the popover is open, and OnClose how it is closed:
    // see [OverlayOptions].
    Open    bool
    OnClose func()
    // Placement is where the popover goes around its trigger, one of
    // Floating UI's 12 placements such as "bottom-start"; "bottom" by
    // default. It flips to the opposite side when there is no room.
    Placement string
    // Offset is the distance in pixels between the trigger and the
    // popover.
    Offset float32
    // Floating are more options of [UseFloating], applied after the
    // popover's own (the placement, [Offset], [Flip] and [Shift] with 12 px
    // of room from the window's edges) and before the arrow's: a [Size]
    // that limits the height to the room available, say.
    Floating []FloatingOption
    // Modal makes the rest of the window inert while the popover is open,
    // as a menu does (React Aria's popovers are modal unless isNonModal
    // is set: here it is the other way round). A press on the trigger then
    // closes the popover, as it hits no element; a non-modal popover does
    // not close for the trigger's presses, which toggle it.
    Modal bool
    // KeyboardDismissDisabled keeps Escape from closing the popover.
    KeyboardDismissDisabled bool
    // ShouldCloseOnInteractOutside decides, for a press outside the popover
    // (and outside the popovers and dialogs opened from it), whether it
    // closes it; nil closes it for every press but the non-modal trigger's.
    ShouldCloseOnInteractOutside func(tela.PointerEvent) bool
    // Ref is the popover element's ref, for a hook used together with
    // others on the same element (the overlay trigger's OverlayRef, a
    // dialog); the zero value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

PopoverOptions configures [`UsePopover`](#func-usepopover).

### type PopoverResult

```go
type PopoverResult struct {
    // Props go to the popover's element: it is fixed to the window and
    // placed next to the trigger in the frame that shows it, it is on the
    // overlay stack (Escape and presses outside close the top one), and
    // the ref. Render the element in a Portal.
    Props tela.Prop
    // ArrowProps go to an arrow element inside the popover, which points at
    // the trigger.
    ArrowProps tela.Prop
    // Placement is the placement the popover is in, after flipping; Side
    // and Align split it. They are the engine's in the frame that shows
    // the popover: see [Floating].
    Placement, Side, Align string
    // Ref is the ref attached to the popover's element by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

PopoverResult is what [`UsePopover`](#func-usepopover) returns.

#### func UsePopover

```go
func UsePopover(o PopoverOptions) PopoverResult
```

UsePopover returns the props of a popover (React Aria's usePopover): a floating element positioned by [`UseFloating`](#func-usefloating) next to its trigger, and dismissed by [`UseOverlay`](#func-useoverlay): Escape, a press outside, or the focus going to another element closes it (never the trigger's press or focus, which toggle it). A press inside a popover opened from it, in a Portal or not, is inside.

```go
trig := aria.UseOverlayTrigger(aria.OverlayTriggerOptions{})
pop := aria.UsePopover(aria.PopoverOptions{
    Trigger: trig.Ref, Ref: trig.OverlayRef, Open: trig.Open, OnClose: trig.Close,
    Placement: "bottom-start", Offset: 4,
})
return Fragment(
    Button(trig.TriggerProps, Text("Filters")),
    Portal(Presence(If(trig.Open,
        Div(pop.Props, Exit("opacity-0"),
            Class("w-64 rounded-md border bg-popover p-4 shadow-md transition starting:opacity-0"),
            Div(pop.ArrowProps, Class("size-2 rotate-45 border bg-popover")),
            Text("Content"))))))
```

Put [`UseDialog`](#func-usedialog) on the same element, sharing the ref, when the popover holds a form or content to be read as a dialog.

**Example**

```go
// A popover 4 px below its trigger; a press outside it closes it.
page := func() tela.Node {
    trig := aria.UseOverlayTrigger(aria.OverlayTriggerOptions{})
    pop := aria.UsePopover(aria.PopoverOptions{
        Trigger: trig.Ref, Ref: trig.OverlayRef, Open: trig.Open, OnClose: trig.Close,
        Placement: "bottom-start", Offset: 4,
    })
    return Div(Class("relative h-full"),
        Button(trig.TriggerProps, Class("absolute left-4 top-4 h-8 w-24"), Text("Filters")),
        Portal(If(trig.Open,
            Div(pop.Props, TestID("pop"), Class("h-24 w-48 rounded-md border bg-white p-2"), Text("Content")))))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(&exampleTB{}, page, telatest.Size(400, 300))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Filters"))
r := app.Bounds(telatest.ByTestID("pop"))
fmt.Printf("popover at (%.0f, %.0f), %.0fx%.0f\n", r.X, r.Y, r.Width, r.Height)
app.ClickAt(350, 250)
app.ExpectNoText("Content")
fmt.Println("closed by a press outside")
// Output:
// popover at (16, 52), 192x96
// closed by a press outside
```

### type PressEvent

```go
type PressEvent struct {
    // PointerType is where the press came from.
    PointerType PointerType
    // X and Y are window coordinates; LocalX and LocalY are relative to the
    // element's border box.
    X, Y, LocalX, LocalY float32
    // Modifier keys held during the event; Meta is the Windows, Command or
    // Super key.
    Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Meta bool
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

PressEvent is passed to the callbacks of [`PressOptions`](#type-pressoptions). X and Y are the position of the event in the window, LocalX and LocalY relative to the border box of the element, in logical pixels; a press that no pointer made (keyboard, virtual) reports the center of the element.

Pressing stops the propagation of the events that make it (the pointer's, the key's, the click), as React Aria does, so a pressable card inside a pressable row presses only the card. Call [`PressEvent.ContinuePropagation`](#func-pressevent-continuepropagation) in a callback to let them bubble.

#### func (PressEvent) ContinuePropagation

```go
func (e PressEvent) ContinuePropagation()
```

ContinuePropagation lets the event that made this press bubble to the ancestors' handlers, instead of stopping it. It applies to the whole step of the press: if any of its callbacks continues, the event does.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var log []string
page := func() tela.Node {
    press := aria.UsePress(aria.PressOptions{
        // Let the card's own handlers see the press too.
        OnPressStart: func(e aria.PressEvent) { e.ContinuePropagation() },
    })
    return Div(OnPointerDown(func() { log = append(log, "the card saw the pointer down") }),
        Button(press.Props, Text("Like")))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Like"))
fmt.Println(log)
// Output: [the card saw the pointer down]
```

### type PressOptions

```go
type PressOptions struct {
    // OnPressStart is called when a press begins: the pointer goes down on
    // the element, or Space goes down on it while it is focused. A press
    // that left the element (without [PressOptions.ShouldCancelOnPointerExit])
    // starts again if the pointer comes back while still held.
    OnPressStart func(PressEvent)
    // OnPressEnd is called when a press ends, whether it counts or not: the
    // release over the element, the pointer leaving it, the cancel of the
    // pointer or a lost focus.
    OnPressEnd func(PressEvent)
    // OnPressChange is called with true when a press starts and false when
    // it ends: the callback form of the Pressed field of the result.
    OnPressChange func(pressed bool)
    // OnPressUp is called when the pointer or the key is released over the
    // element, before OnPressEnd.
    OnPressUp func(PressEvent)
    // OnPress is called when the press completes: the release over the
    // element, Space released on it, Enter pressed on it, or a virtual
    // click. It does not run for a disabled element.
    OnPress func(PressEvent)
    // Disabled ignores every pointer, key and click on the element, and
    // ends a press in progress. It sets no prop: for a disabled look and
    // semantics use [UseButton] or h.Disabled.
    Disabled bool
    // ShouldCancelOnPointerExit ends the press for good when the pointer
    // leaves the element, instead of letting it start again when the
    // pointer comes back while pressed.
    ShouldCancelOnPointerExit bool
    // PreventFocusOnPress keeps the focus where it is when the pointer
    // goes down on the element (the default action of a press is to focus
    // the nearest focusable element).
    PreventFocusOnPress bool
    // Ref is the element's ref, for a hook that is used together with
    // others on one element (see the package documentation); the zero
    // value makes the hook create its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

PressOptions configures [`UsePress`](#func-usepress).

### type PressResult

```go
type PressResult struct {
    // Props go to the element: the pointer, key, click and blur handlers
    // and the ref, merged. Props given after them in the element's
    // arguments override what they set, but handlers of the same event all
    // run.
    Props tela.Prop
    // Pressed is true while the element is pressed (a pointer is down on
    // it, or Space is held): style it with a class, since `active:` follows
    // the pointer only.
    Pressed bool
    // Ref is the ref attached to the element by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

PressResult is what [`UsePress`](#func-usepress) returns.

#### func UsePress

```go
func UsePress(o PressOptions) PressResult
```

UsePress returns the props that make an element pressable, the same across mouse, touch, pen and keyboard (React Aria's usePress).

```go
press := aria.UsePress(aria.PressOptions{
    OnPress: func(e aria.PressEvent) { save() },
    Disabled: busy,
})
return Div(press.Props, Role("button"), TabIndex(0),
    Class("rounded-md px-3 py-1.5"), If(press.Pressed, Class("scale-95")), Text("Save"))
```

A press starts when the primary button, a touch contact or a pen tip goes down on the element. It ends when the pointer is released ([`PressOptions.OnPress`](#type-pressoptions) runs if that was over the element), leaves the element (which also ends it for good with [`PressOptions.ShouldCancelOnPointerExit`](#type-pressoptions)) or is cancelled: the system takes the touch, a touch becomes a scroll, or the element is unmounted. The element keeps receiving the pointer while it is pressed, wherever it goes.

With the keyboard, Enter on the focused element presses it at once (OnPressStart, OnPressUp, OnPressEnd and OnPress on the key down, never on a repeat), and Space starts the press on the key down and completes it on the key up; a press by Space ends without OnPress when the focus leaves the element. The hook prevents the default action of those keys (the click of a Button, the scroll of Space). A click that no pointer made (an assistive technology, an agent, a Label) is a virtual press.

The hook stops the propagation of the events that make a press (PressEvent.ContinuePropagation lets them bubble), prevents the default action of the click (a Button does not submit its Form), and does not run for a Disabled element.

The element needs no role: UsePress adds none. For a button use [`UseButton`](#func-usebutton), which adds the role, the tab stop and the disabled state.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
save := func() tela.Node {
    saved, setSaved := tela.UseState(0)
    press := aria.UsePress(aria.PressOptions{
        OnPress: func(e aria.PressEvent) { setSaved.Update(func(n int) int { return n + 1 }) },
    })
    return Div(press.Props, Role("button"), TabIndex(0),
        Class("rounded-md px-3 py-1.5"), If(press.Pressed, Class("scale-95")),
        Textf("Saved %d times", saved))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, save)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Saved 0 times"))
app.Press("Enter") // the button has the focus after the click
app.Press("Space")
app.ExpectText("Saved 3 times")
fmt.Println("3 presses: mouse, Enter, Space")
// Output: 3 presses: mouse, Enter, Space
```

### type ProgressBarOptions

```go
type ProgressBarOptions struct {
    // Value is the progress, from Min to Max. It is ignored while
    // Indeterminate.
    Value float64
    // Min and Max are the ends of the scale. Min is 0 by default and Max
    // 100 when both are 0.
```

### type RadioGroupOptions

```go
type RadioGroupOptions[K comparable] struct {
    // Keys are the keys of the radios, in the order they are shown. The
    // list must be given on every build.
    Keys []K
    // DisabledKeys are the radios that can not be focused or checked.
    // They are skipped by the arrow keys, and get Disabled and
    // AriaDisabled.
    DisabledKeys []K
    // Value points to the checked key of a controlled group; nil leaves
    // the value to the hook.
    Value *K
    // DefaultValue is the checked key of an uncontrolled group at the
    // start; nil checks nothing.
    DefaultValue *K
    // OnValueChange is called with the next key when the user checks a
    // radio: for a controlled group it is how the change is asked for, for
    // an uncontrolled one a notification. It is not called for the radio
    // that already is checked.
    OnValueChange func(K)
    // Disabled disables every radio.
    Disabled bool
    // ReadOnly keeps the radios focusable but not changeable
    // (aria-readonly on the group).
    ReadOnly bool
    // Required marks the group as one the user must answer
    // (aria-required).
    Required bool
    // Orientation is "vertical" (the default, as React Aria's) or
    // "horizontal". It is aria-orientation, and decides whether a
    // right-to-left Direction swaps ArrowLeft and ArrowRight: all four
    // arrows move the focus in either orientation.
    Orientation string
    // Direction is "ltr" (the default) or "rtl".
    Direction string
    // AriaLabel names the group; else it is named by the element with
    // LabelProps, or by AriaLabelledBy.
    AriaLabel string
    // AriaLabelledBy is the element that names the group, when it is not
    // the one with LabelProps.
    AriaLabelledBy tela.ElementRef
    // Ref is the group element's ref, for a hook that is used together
    // with others on one element; the zero value makes the hook create
    // its own.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
}
```

RadioGroupOptions configures [`UseRadioGroup`](#func-useradiogroup). K is the type of the radios' keys: a string, an int, an enum; any comparable value.

The value is uncontrolled when Value is nil (the hook keeps it, starting at DefaultValue, or with nothing checked) and controlled when Value points to the caller's state: the group shows it and only asks OnValueChange for the next one, so a change the caller does not store is refused. OnValueChange is also called for an uncontrolled group. A value that is not one of Keys (a controlled "" for none) checks no radio.

```go
// Uncontrolled, starting at "pro".
aria.RadioGroupOptions[string]{Keys: plans, DefaultValue: new("pro")}
// Controlled.
plan, setPlan := tela.UseState("pro")
aria.RadioGroupOptions[string]{Keys: plans, Value: &plan, OnValueChange: setPlan.Set}
```

### type RadioGroupResult

```go
type RadioGroupResult[K comparable] struct {
    // Props go to the group's element: the "radiogroup" role,
    // aria-orientation, its name, the required, read-only and disabled
    // states and the ref.
    Props tela.Prop
    // LabelProps go to the element that labels the group (a span or a
    // Label): its text names the group, unless AriaLabel is set.
    LabelProps tela.Prop
    // Value is the checked key, valid when HasValue is true. It can be a
    // key that is not one of Keys when a controlled group says so.
    Value K
    // HasValue is whether the group has a value.
    HasValue bool
    // Ref is the ref attached to the group by Props.
    Ref tela.ElementRef
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

RadioGroupResult is what [`UseRadioGroup`](#func-useradiogroup) returns.

#### func UseRadioGroup

```go
func UseRadioGroup[K comparable](o RadioGroupOptions[K]) RadioGroupResult[K]
```

UseRadioGroup holds the state of a radio group and returns the props of the group and its radios (React Aria's useRadioGroup and useRadio with react-stately's useRadioGroupState). At most one radio is checked; the caller renders one element per key.

```go
plan := aria.UseRadioGroup(aria.RadioGroupOptions[string]{Keys: plans, DefaultValue: new("free"), AriaLabel: "Plan"})
return Div(plan.Props, Class("grid gap-2"),
    h.Range(len(plans), func(i int) tela.Node {
        k := plans[i]
        return Div(Key(k), Class("flex items-center gap-2"),
            Button(plan.RadioProps(k), Class("size-4 rounded-full border checked:bg-primary")),
            Label(For(plan.RadioID(k)), Text(k)))
    }))
```

The arrow keys (all four, in either orientation) move the focus to the next enabled radio, going around the ends, and check it; Space checks the focused radio; Tab enters the group at the checked radio. A press checks a radio. Right-to-left Direction swaps the horizontal arrows.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
plans := []string{"free", "pro", "team"}
page := func() tela.Node {
    g := aria.UseRadioGroup(aria.RadioGroupOptions[string]{Keys: plans, DefaultValue: new("free"), AriaLabel: "Plan"})
    return Div(g.Props, Class("flex flex-col gap-1"),
        Range(len(plans), func(i int) tela.Node {
            k := plans[i]
            return Div(Key(k), Class("flex items-center gap-2"),
                Button(g.RadioProps(k), Class("size-4 rounded-full border checked:bg-primary")),
                Label(For(g.RadioID(k)), Text(k)))
        }))
}
app := telatest.MountFunc(t, page)
app.Focus(telatest.ByRole("radio", "free"))
app.Press("ArrowDown") // moves the focus and checks
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - radiogroup "Plan":
//   - radio "free"
//   - text: free
//   - radio "pro" [checked]
//   - text: pro
//   - radio "team"
//   - text: team
```

#### func (RadioGroupResult[K]) IsSelected

```go
func (r RadioGroupResult[K]) IsSelected(k K) bool
```

IsSelected reports whether the radio with key k is the checked one.

#### func (RadioGroupResult[K]) RadioID

```go
func (r RadioGroupResult[K]) RadioID(k K) string
```

RadioID returns the id that RadioProps(k) gives the radio, for a Label's For.

#### func (RadioGroupResult[K]) RadioProps

```go
func (r RadioGroupResult[K]) RadioProps(k K) tela.Prop
```

RadioProps returns the props of the radio with key k (React Aria's useRadio): the "radio" role, aria-checked, an ID for a Label, the ref, a tab stop on the checked radio (the first enabled one while none is checked; the arrow keys move between the others), the disabled state and the handlers: a click, tap or Space checks it, and the arrow keys move the focus to the next radio and check it.

Render the radio with a Button: a Label(For(RadioID(k))) then names it and checks it when it is clicked. A Div works too, but a Label only names it. The `checked:` variant (and `aria-checked:`) match the checked radio.

#### func (RadioGroupResult[K]) RadioRef

```go
func (r RadioGroupResult[K]) RadioRef(k K) tela.ElementRef
```

RadioRef returns the ref that RadioProps(k) attaches to the radio, to share with another hook on its element.

### type RangeCalendarOptions

```go
type RangeCalendarOptions struct {
    // Value points to the selected range of a controlled calendar; nil
    // leaves it to the hook. DefaultValue starts an uncontrolled one,
    // and OnValueChange is called with the range the user completes (the
    // earlier date first). The zero DateRange selects nothing.
    Value         *DateRange
    DefaultValue  DateRange
    OnValueChange func(DateRange)
    // AllowsNonContiguousRanges lets a range cross unavailable dates.
    // Without it, once the first date is chosen the dates beyond the
    // nearest unavailable one on each side are unavailable too, so a
    // range never contains one (React Aria's rule). The nearest one is
    // searched three years either way.
    AllowsNonContiguousRanges bool

    Min, Max           Date
    IsDateUnavailable  func(Date) bool
    Disabled           bool
    ReadOnly           bool
    FocusedDate        *Date
    DefaultFocusedDate Date
    OnFocusChange      func(Date)
    VisibleMonths      int
    FirstDayOfWeek     *time.Weekday
    FixedWeeks         bool
    Today              Date
    Locale             string
    Direction          string
    AriaLabel          string
    AriaLabelledBy     tela.ElementRef
    PreviousLabel      string
    NextLabel          string
    Ref                tela.ElementRef
}
```

RangeCalendarOptions configures [`UseRangeCalendar`](#func-userangecalendar). The fields shared with [`CalendarOptions`](#type-calendaroptions) mean the same; the value is a [`DateRange`](#type-daterange).
